title: Control interno y gestión de riesgos financieros: revisión bibliométrica y síntesis temática con implicaciones conceptuales para el sector cooperativo
summary: The objective of this study was to analyze the evolution and conceptual structure of the scientific literature identified at the explicit intersection of internal control and financial risk, and to synthesize its conceptual implications for credit unions. A literature review was conducted using a quantitative approach with a descriptive-bibliometric scope. Data were obtained from Scopus using the TITLE-ABS-KEY search equation (“financial risk” AND “internal control”), applied on July 4, 2026, to articles published through 2026. The identification and selection process was reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and resulted in a final corpus of 64 articles published between 1991 and 2026. The analysis incorporated temporal evolution, bibliometric mapping using PHAROS METRIX NEXT, and a thematic synthesis of the 64 records. The results showed a recent expansion of the field: 39 articles (60.9%) were concentrated between 2024 and 2026. The conceptual framework revealed recurring links between financial risk, internal control, corporate governance, auditing, financial reporting, fraud, digital transformation, and sustainability. The integrative synthesis, compared with the COSO framework, organized the evidence into four dimensions: control and governance environment; comprehensive risk identification and measurement; control, audit, and remediation activities; and information, technology, and communication. These dimensions are not presented as an empirically validated model, but rather as a conceptual adaptation that facilitates the prudent transfer of heterogeneous findings to the cooperative sector. It is concluded that the literature offers a useful basis for guiding future research and the design of control and risk management systems in cooperatives, without constituting direct evidence of effectiveness in these entities.

title: Digital Transformation and Green Innovation in Construction Enterprises: The Mediating Role of Green Dynamic Capability and Moderating Effect of Command-and-Control Environmental Regulation
summary: As the digital economy expands rapidly, intelligent-green synergy among construction enterprises has become an inevitable path toward industrial sustainable development, with green innovation acting as its core anchor. Based on the resource-based view, this paper conducts a questionnaire survey on construction enterprises and collects 288 valid questionnaires to empirically examine the influencing mechanism of digital transformation on green innovation in construction enterprises. The results show that the digital transformation of construction enterprises is significantly positively associated with green innovation. Green dynamic capability (GDC) exerts a significant positive mediating effect. Specifically, digital transformation exhibits a positive link with green innovation by enhancing GDC. Meanwhile, command-and-control environmental regulation positively moderates the association between digital transformation and green innovation. Furthermore, a higher level of command-and-control environmental regulation also strengthens the mediating effect transmitted by GDC. Drawing on the above conclusions, this paper proposes suggestions to promote the high-quality development of construction enterprises by deepening green digital transformation, fostering GDC, and leveraging the dividends of command-and-control environmental regulation. The research findings provide theoretical and practical foundations for construction enterprises to seize digital opportunities and fully implement green innovation strategies.

title: The Effect of Environmental Management Accounting on Company Performance Through Green Innovation with Stakeholder Pressure as A Moderation Variable in Companies in The Basic Industry and Chemical Sectors Listed on The Indonesia Stock Exchange For The Period 2021-2025
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of environmental management accounting (EMA) on firm performance through green innovation as an intervening variable, with stakeholder pressure as a moderating variable in basic materials and chemical sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2021–2025. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data from annual reports and sustainability reports. The population consists of all basic materials and chemical sector companies listed on the IDX, and purposive sampling yielded 44 companies or 220 firm-year observations. EMA is measured using an environmental management accounting disclosure index, green innovation is measured using a green product and process innovation index, stakeholder pressure is measured using a composite stakeholder-pressure index, and firm performance is measured using return on assets (ROA). Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The results show that EMA has a significant positive effect on firm performance (β = 0.238, p < 0.001) and on green innovation (β = 0.356, p < 0.001); green innovation has a significant positive effect on firm performance (β = 0.312, p < 0.001) and partially mediates the effect of EMA on firm performance (VAF = 31.8%); and stakeholder pressure significantly strengthens the effect of green innovation on firm performance (interaction β = 0.176, p < 0.01). These findings imply that stakeholder pressure plays an important role in strengthening the contribution of green innovation to improved firm performance

title: Mission command and supply chain resilience in wartime military logistics: empirical evidence from the Ukrainian Armed Forces
summary: Purpose This study investigates how command, control and leadership mechanisms enable supply chain resilience (SCRES) in wartime military logistics, addressing a gap in empirical research on organizational and command factors under adversarial conditions. Design/methodology/approach We collected survey data (n = 82) from logistics experts in the Ukrainian Armed Forces (UAF) and analyzed the structural relationships among mission command (MC), leader–member exchange (LMX), planning (PLAN), visibility (VIS), responsiveness (RESP) and recovery (REC) using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) combined with necessary condition analysis (NCA). Findings The structural model yielded predictive relevance (R2 RESP = 0.705, R2 REC = 0.415). RESP emerged as the strongest predictor of REC (β = 0.542), the central mediating pathway to resilience outcomes. MC strongly predicted RESP (β = 0.477), indirectly influencing REC through this pathway. MC and RESP showed close empirical overlap, plausibly reflecting MC's doctrinal role in producing responsiveness, though this warrants cautious interpretation. LMX strengthened resilience indirectly by supporting MC. NCA revealed that VIS and MC function as necessary conditions for achieving high REC, even when their direct effects are nonsignificant in SEM. Originality/value By integrating PLS-SEM with NCA, we offer a leadership-centered explanation of SCRES in wartime military operations. The findings are consistent with perceptual evidence of NATO-aligned MC practices among surveyed UAF logistics personnel, underscoring their role in sustaining supply chain resilience. These insights primarily inform military logistics, with potential relevance for how command-and-control affects resilience in other high-stakes environments.

title: Beyond Board Governance: Does the External Governance Ecosystem Enhance Corporate Value in Emerging Markets? Evidence from Listed Nigerian Banking Institutions
summary: Purpose This study investigates whether the external governance ecosystem enhances the corporate value of listed Nigerian banking institutions. Moving beyond the traditional board-centric approach, it examines the influence of regulatory oversight, external audit quality, and environmental governance as complementary external governance mechanisms operating through monitoring, credibility, and legitimacy channels. Methodology/Approach The study draws on agency, institutional, and stakeholder theories and employs a longitudinal panel design covering 11 listed Nigerian banking institutions over the period 2012-2025. Using 154 firm-year observations, Tobin’s Q serves as the measure of corporate value. The Prais-Winsten Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) estimator is applied to address heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, and cross-sectional dependence. Firm size, leverage, and profitability are included as control variables. Findings The results reveal that regulatory oversight has a positive but statistically insignificant effect on corporate value, while external audit quality and environmental governance exhibit negative but insignificant effects. Among the control variables, firm size and leverage significantly reduce corporate value, whereas profitability has a positive but insignificant relationship with firm value. The findings suggest that external governance arrangements do not automatically generate market valuation benefits within emerging-market banking institutions. Originality/Value The study contributes to corporate governance literature by introducing an external governance ecosystem perspective that conceptualizes regulatory oversight, external audit quality, and environmental governance as interconnected governance institutions rather than isolated mechanisms. It also extends evidence from the underexplored context of Nigerian banking institutions and emerging markets. Practical Implications The findings highlight the importance of strengthening governance enforcement, disclosure credibility, and sustainability integration. Regulators, managers, and investors should focus on governance effectiveness rather than formal compliance, as external governance mechanisms appear to contribute more to transparency, accountability, and institutional legitimacy than to immediate market valuation gains.

title: Assessing the Influence of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Adoption on Financial Transparency and Investor Confidence
summary: This systematic literature review synthesizes evidence on the association between International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) adoption and two outcome domains: financial transparency and financial reporting quality, and investor confidence and capital-market outcomes. The review draws on 41 empirical, conceptual, and review-based studies across multiple institutional and geopolitical contexts. The assessment focuses on empirical evidence indicating that IFRS implementation is frequently associated with improvements in financial reporting quality, especially in terms of comparability and transparency. The reviewed literature also suggests that these reporting improvements may support investor confidence and capital-market development, although the magnitude and consistency of these associations vary across institutional settings. Evidence further indicates that IFRS-related benefits are conditional on regulatory enforcement, institutional quality, corporate governance, organizational readiness, and regional stability. Barriers such as limited professional capacity, technical complexity, training costs, and geopolitical uncertainty can restrict reform effectiveness, particularly in developing and conflict-affected economies. The review contributes by integrating reporting and investor-facing outcomes, highlighting boundary conditions that explain divergent findings, and identifying future research gaps related to non-financial metrics, ESG reporting, longitudinal effects, and IFRS adoption in unstable institutional contexts. The paper concludes that IFRS adoption can support global financial harmonization, but its benefits depend on complementary institutions, effective enforcement, and local contextual fit.

title: Integrasi Prinsip Maqāṣid Al-Syarī‘Ah Dan Environmental,Social, Governance (Esg) Dalam Penilaian Kelayakan Investasi Saham Syariah
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis integrasi prinsip Maqāṣid al-Syarī‘ah dan Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) dalam penilaian kelayakan investasi saham syariah di Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan deskriptif-analitis melalui library research dan analisis dokumen. Data diperoleh dari Al-Qur’an, hadis, fatwa DSN-MUI, regulasi Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK), dokumen resmi, serta literatur ilmiah yang relevan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa mekanisme screening saham syariah yang selama ini menekankan aspek kegiatan usaha dan rasio keuangan dapat diperluas dengan memasukkan dimensi ESG yang selaras dengan tujuan Maqāṣid al-Syarī‘ah. Maqāṣid al-Syarī‘ah berfungsi sebagai landasan normatif dan etis yang berorientasi pada kemaslahatan, sedangkan ESG menjadi instrumen operasional untuk menilai tanggung jawab perusahaan terhadap lingkungan, masyarakat, dan tata kelola. Integrasi keduanya menunjukkan adanya keterkaitan antara ḥifẓ al-nafs dengan aspek environmental dan social, serta ḥifẓ al-māl dengan aspek governance. Dengan demikian, integrasi Maqāṣid al-Syarī‘ah dan ESG dapat membentuk kerangka penilaian investasi saham syariah yang lebih holistik, tidak hanya berorientasi pada kepatuhan syariah dan kinerja finansial, tetapi juga mempertimbangkan keberlanjutan, keadilan, tanggung jawab sosial, dan kemaslahatan masyarakat.

title: Sustainable Finance and the Reallocation of Capital for Ecological Transition
summary: This paper examines the role of sustainable finance in supporting green investment and financing the ecological transition. It reviews three interconnected dimensions: the integration of environmental, social and governance criteria into investment decisions and asset pricing; the development of green financial instruments and financial intermediation; and the financing mechanisms supporting renewable energy, public green investment and corporate transition. The literature indicates that sustainability considerations increasingly affect investor behavior, capital allocation, risk assessment and financing costs, although their financial consequences remain heterogeneous across markets and institutional settings. ESG information can redirect investment flows, but disagreements among rating providers and differences in materiality limit the reliability of sustainability signals. Green bonds, green credit and sustainable banking mechanisms can facilitate environmental investment, yet their effectiveness depends on certification, disclosure quality, liquidity, policy credibility and borrower characteristics. Public financial institutions also play an important role in absorbing early-stage risks, creating markets and mobilizing private capital for low-carbon technologies. The reviewed evidence further shows that climate transition requires more than specialized green instruments. Financial-system structure, corporate investment decisions, regulatory frameworks and coordinated public policies influence whether capital is effectively redirected toward environmentally sustainable activities. Sustainable finance therefore represents an evolving institutional framework through which environmental objectives, financial risk and long-term investment are progressively integrated.

title: Green accounting and governance capability configurations for sustainability performance in resource constrained environmental governance
summary: Environmental governance research suggests that well-designed sustainability practices can strengthen organizational resilience. Yet public institutions and communities under institutional scarcity may be unable to develop all desirable technological, financial, and managerial capabilities simultaneously. Drawing on Resource Orchestration Theory (ROT), this study examines how Green Accounting, Social Capital, Digital Capability, and Governance Agility combine in relation to Sustainability Performance. Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) of questionnaire data from 152 respondents in Kendari City, Indonesia, identifies three configurations that satisfy the stated sufficiency-retention criteria (primary solution consistency = 0.868; coverage = 0.714) and one additional digital-absence pattern with borderline PRI consistency (0.695), which is treated as exploratory rather than as part of the primary solution. The fully integrated configuration has the highest raw coverage (0.539). Governance Agility narrowly crosses the conventional necessity benchmark (consistency = 0.907; coverage = 0.774), but this near-threshold result is sample-specific; no condition is sufficient alone. Alternative Triple Bottom Line weights produce primary-solution coverage of 0.712–0.715 and consistency of 0.864–0.872. The findings provide a bounded refinement of ROT by treating institutional scarcity as a contextual constraint on feasible capability orchestration and by distinguishing complementary from functionally compensatory capability alignment. Compensation denotes overlapping governance functions, not universal resource substitution. The results support contextual inference for Kendari and require comparison, rather than direct generalization, in other institutional environments.

title: Mediterranean cruise tourism: shore excursions and corporate social responsibility
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how corporate social responsibility (CSR) can be represented as a cybernetic control mechanism within shore excursion systems in Mediterranean cruise tourism. It aims to explore how feedback structures may influence tour operator reputation, environmental sustainability and guest satisfaction in complex destination systems. Design/methodology/approach The study integrates cybernetic theory with system dynamics modelling. A causal loop diagram and stock-and-flow simulation model were developed through Group Model Building and expert-based calibration. Scenario simulations were conducted for three Adriatic cruise destinations – Trieste, Koper and Dubrovnik – to explore system behaviour under different CSR implementation conditions. Findings The simulations illustrate how different configurations of CSR implementation and organisational capabilities may influence system behaviour over time. Within the model, stronger CSR implementation and stakeholder capabilities are associated with reinforcing dynamics linked to reputation, environmental sustainability and guest satisfaction. Research limitations/implications The results should be interpreted as model-generated scenarios rather than empirical predictions. As the model relies on expert-based calibration and destination-specific assumptions, future research should incorporate broader empirical data sets and test the framework in different cruise tourism contexts. Practical implications The model provides a scenario-testing and decision-support tool that can help destination managers, tour operators and policymakers evaluate alternative CSR strategies, identify potential trade-offs and anticipate long-term system responses. Originality/value This study contributes primarily at the methodological level by integrating cybernetic theory, system dynamics modelling, group model building and expert-based calibration into a coherent framework for analysing CSR dynamics in cruise tourism and shore excursion management.

title: The Illusion of Readiness: Deconstructing Performative Compliance in Supply Chain Digital Transformation
summary: Digital transformation has become a critical strategy for improving supply chain resilience, operational efficiency, and organizational competitiveness. However, significant investments in digital technologies do not always produce proportional improvements in operational outcomes, creating a productivity paradox in which technological adoption exceeds actual utilization. This study aims to examine the behavioral mechanisms underlying Digital Transformation Implementation (DTI) by investigating the roles of Perceived Usefulness (PU), Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU), and Employees’ Intentional Digital Readiness (EIDR) among supply chain personnel. This study employed a quantitative cross-sectional research design using a structured questionnaire distributed to employees involved in supply chain and logistics functions within Indonesian manufacturing firms and logistics service providers. Data from 247 valid respondents were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings reveal that Perceived Usefulness and Perceived Ease of Use significantly influence Digital Transformation Implementation, indicating that employees primarily adopt digital systems when they provide practical benefits and operational convenience. Conversely, Employees’ Intentional Digital Readiness does not significantly affect implementation, suggesting a gap between employees’ expressed readiness and actual digital adoption behavior. The study concludes that successful supply chain digital transformation depends more on technological utility and usability than psychological readiness alone. These findings contribute to digital transformation literature by highlighting the importance of evaluating actual operational integration rather than relying solely on self-reported readiness indicators.

title: Extraterritorial ESG regulation and mining governance in Peru: Risks of a legislative disconnect
summary: Peru is one of the world's most important mining economies and a strategic supplier of copper, silver, tin, zinc, lead, gold, and molybdenum. Yet the governance conditions under which Peruvian minerals enter global markets are changing rapidly. A new generation of mandatory sustainability rules, especially in the European Union, is shifting mining governance from voluntary corporate social responsibility toward auditable environmental, social, and governance (ESG) assurance across global value chains. This Perspective examines the resulting legislative disconnect between Peru's domestic mining framework, which remains strongly oriented toward site-based environmental licensing, impact assessment, and local conflict management, and the emerging audit-driven paradigm of value-chain traceability, human rights due diligence, greenhouse gas accounting, and sustainability reporting. Drawing on comparative institutional analysis, selected legal and policy instruments, and illustrative evidence from large-scale mining operators, the article develops a conceptual ESG risk-mapping framework for Peruvian mining exports. The argument is not that Peruvian law is irrelevant or weak in all respects, but that domestic compliance is no longer sufficient for maintaining commercial legitimacy in markets where buyers, lenders, insurers, and commodity traders face their own reporting and due diligence obligations. The paper contributes to debates in resource governance by showing how extraterritorial regulation can operate through contracts, finance, and trading hubs, thereby creating new forms of market access risk for mineral-rich economies. It concludes by proposing policy measures to strengthen ESG data capacity, sectoral traceability, and assurance-oriented mining governance in Peru.

title: Climate Risk Disclosure, Green Finance, and Cost of Capital Among PSX Non-Financial Firms
summary: ABSTRACT: Purpose: The purpose of this study is to examine correlations between climate risk disclosure quality (CRDI), green finance (GFI), and cost of capital (COC) among Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX)-based non-financial companies for 2013-2023. The study is based on Information Asymmetry Theory, Stakeholder Theory and Legitimacy Theory to investigate whether superior climate risk disclosure leads to lower cost of equity, debt and WACC; whether green finance acts as a mediator in the context of the aforementioned relationship; and whether board environmental expertise acts as a moderator in the mediated pathway. Design/Methodology/Approach: An unbalanced panel of 165 PSX-listed non-financial firms (maximum 1,815 firm-year observations) is analyzed. The Climate Risk Disclosure Index (CRDI) is a 24-item index based on structured content analysis (dual-coder, Cohen's Kappa = 0.83), which can be disaggregated to include the categories of transition risk disclosure (TRD), physical risk disclosure (PRD), and governance climate accountability (GCA). Cost of equity is calculated by using CAPM, cost of debt by using the interest expense ratio and WACC by using the market-value weighting. Green finance is expressed in a PCA-weighted combination of four instruments. Endogeneity is controlled for using System GMM (Blundell and Bond, 1998). Estimation of mediation (PROCESS Model 4) and moderated mediation (PROCESS Model 14) involves the use of BCa bootstrapped confidence intervals (5000 iterations). Findings: CRDI is negatively and significantly associated with cost of equity (beta = -0.187, p < 0.001), cost of debt (beta = -0.142, p < 0.001), and WACC (beta = -0.168, p < 0.001). The CRDI-cost of equity relationship is partially mediated by green finance (indirect effect = -0.072; BCa 95% CI [-0.118, -0.031]), accounting for nearly 38.5% of the total. Highly-efficient boards (IMM = -0.024; BCa 95% CI [-0.041, -0.009]) provide significant moderation of this mediated pathway, reducing costs by 2.1x more. Other disclosure variables, including transition risk disclosure (beta = -0.214), have higher effects on capital costs than do physical risk disclosure (beta = -0.156). All results are robust to GMM endogeneity correction. Research Limitations: Single-country PSX setting; GRI content-analysis-based CRDI is based on self-disclosed reports; limited data availability on green finance after 2023 for SECP-mandatory PE disclosures; and availability of data for the era before SECP-mandatory PE disclosures is limited. Practical Implications: Ensure that SECP require TCFD related disclosures by PSX companies. To incentivize green finance cost reduction, environmental expertise investment is needed in boards. SBP Sustainable Finance Framework certification is a capital cost optimizing strategy outside of regulation. Originality/Value: It is the first study which provide the TCFD-aligned CRDI for PSX non-financial firms disaggregating TRD, PRD, and GCA; (2) it is the first study to find evidence of CRDI-COC through the mediation of green finance; (3) it is the first study to test Board EE as a moderator; and (4) it is the most comprehensive PSX decade panel climate disclosure and capital costs with System GMM correction. Keywords: climate risk disclosure; green finance; cost of capital; TCFD; board environmental expertise; PSX; WACC; information asymmetry; System GMM; emerging markets

title: Artificial intelligence in sustainable supply chain resilience with predictive analytics as a mediator and environmental uncertainty as a moderator
summary: Abstract Recent disruptions caused by pandemics, climate change, and geopolitical conflicts have exposed the vulnerability of supply chains, particularly in developing economies with limited digital infrastructure. This study investigates how artificial intelligence can increase sustainable supply chain resilience through predictive analytics. It explores the influence of environmental uncertainty on sustainable supply chain resilience in Bangladesh’s manufacturing and pharmaceutical industries. Data were collected from 372 managers of manufacturing and pharmaceutical industries in the Dhaka and Chattogram divisions. PLS-SEM was used to analyze the proposed model in SmartPLS 4. MGA was also performed to compare the structures in the two sectors. Results showed that the use of AI has a positive impact on predictive analytics (β = 0.36, p < 0.001) and sustainable supply chain resilience (β = 0.17, p < 0.001). Predictive analytics also has a significant positive effect on sustainable supply chain resilience (β = 0.36, p < 0.001) and partially mediates the relationship between AI and resilience (β = 0.13, p < 0.001). There is a negative moderating effect of environmental uncertainty on the connection between AI and resilience (β = − 0.13, p = 0.001). The model explains 13% of the variance in predictive analytics and 58% in sustainable supply chain resilience. A second analysis of the results across the different groups indicates that the negative moderating impact of environmental uncertainty is significantly greater in the manufacturing sector than in the pharmaceutical sector. This study extends the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory by conceptualizing AI as a strategic technological resource. Predictive analytics is conceptualized as an organizational capability. It illustrates that analytical power is the key component of AI for creating resilience, but certain environmental variables may determine its success. This study combines mediation, moderation, and sectoral comparisons, providing realistic and useful insights for managers and policymakers in emerging markets.

title: From ESG to Biodiversity: Decoupling and Its Asymmetries as a Source of Biodiversity Risk
summary: ABSTRACT While environmental, social and governance (ESG) research has extensively documented the risks stemming from disclosure and performance gaps, the growing demand for biodiversity reporting raises concerns that analogous inconsistencies may amplify corporations' exposure to biodiversity risk. Using a sample of 917 firm‐year observations from 2015 to 2023, this study examines whether biodiversity decoupling, the divergence between biodiversity disclosure and performance, is associated with corporations' exposure to biodiversity risk. Drawing on the legitimacy theory, we find that higher levels of biodiversity decoupling are associated with increased biodiversity risk. However, when distinguishing between the types of decoupling, we observe no significant association for positive decoupling, whereas negative decoupling is associated with lower biodiversity risk, suggesting that disclosure‐performance gaps operate differently in the context of biodiversity. We further show that environmental audit moderates the relationship between biodiversity decoupling and biodiversity risk by attenuating the association of positive biodiversity decoupling and the risk‐reduction association of negative biodiversity decoupling. Overall, our findings offer timely insights for corporations seeking to manage legitimacy pressures, for investors aiming to understand the drivers of biodiversity risk and for policymakers wishing to develop more robust biodiversity reporting standards.

title: A novel smart partial least squares-based model for analyzing key factors driving green finance and accounting companies’ performance in big data era
summary: Sustainability in the business world, particularly in the financial sector, entails adopting strategies and practices that benefit both the environment and society, while also ensuring the profitability and financial growth of companies. This concept is becoming a critical factor in assessing green financial performance, as companies that adhere to sustainability principles can manage their resources more efficiently and are more resilient to environmental and economic changes. The analysis of large data sets through big data technologies enables companies to collect extensive environmental, social, and economic information, supporting more informed sustainable practice decisions. Green finance is a relatively new concept that offers an option for green financing to individuals, corporate entities, and governments that are willing to finance and invest in green activities or low-carbon initiatives. The use of big data in green finance facilitates a more accurate assessment of investment opportunities and risks associated with green and low-carbon projects. This paper proposes the Smart Partial Least Squares model to investigate the performance and growth determinants of green finance and accounting firms. As green practices gain traction in the financial industry, it becomes crucial to identify the factors that explain the success of green finance. The proposed model considers both technology-based changes and managerial perspectives in evaluating the key performance drivers. Big data technologies, such as machine learning and artificial intelligence, can be leveraged to gain a deeper understanding of the impact these drivers have on green finance and accounting firms. The results indicate that both internal factors (technological variables and management variables) and external factors (economic variables, legal and regulatory variables) significantly contribute to the growth and efficiency of green finance firms, providing valuable insights for practitioners and policymakers. The research results show that this interaction between internal and external factors is effective in creating a positive cycle between sustainability and green financial performance, which can lead to sustainable and long-term growth of companies in competitive markets. Managers should note that any improvement in ICT application may contribute meaningfully to the overall performance of green finance and accounting firms. This research will contribute to the literature on the performance of green finance and accounting companies by integrating all the mentioned variables, including the role of big data in optimising green finance strategies.

title: Stakeholder-Centric Corporate Social Responsibility: Creating Shared Value Through Strategic Engagement
summary: The notion of corporate social responsibility (CSR) has evolved from an ancillary activity of philanthropy to a strategic approach towards building trust, reputation, and relationship with stakeholders. This research examines the perception of CSR awareness, perceived authenticity, stakeholder engagement, and creation of shared value, and its associations with the variables of trust, reputation, satisfaction/loyalty and behavioral intentions. The data collection instrument comprised 24 items in Likert-type scale form and measured eight variables. The reliability of the measures was checked using Cronbach's alpha, while the Pearson correlation, ordinary least squares (OLS) regression, one-way ANOVA, and independent sample t-test were used for statistical analysis. All Cronbach's alphas fell within the range .67 to .77, showing acceptable reliability, and construct means ranged from 3.52 to 3.70. However, none of the proposed hypotheses was supported, since correlations were weak and statistically insignificant (|r| < .13), and explained less than 4% of variance in satisfaction/loyalty and behavioral intentions (all p > .50). Satisfaction and loyalty significantly differed among different age groups (p = .023), with younger respondents expressing greater satisfaction and loyalty, while there was marginally significant gender difference in stakeholder engagement (p = .085). There were no significant differences by any other demographic variable or stakeholder type.

title: Examining the Impact of Corporate Social Responsibility on Financial Performance: Evidence from Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Hanoi
summary: This study examines the effect of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on the financial performance (FP) of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Hanoi, Vietnam, through the mediating role of corporate reputation (REP). Drawing on stakeholder theory, signaling theory, the resource-based view, legitimacy theory, and the creating-shared-value perspective, CSR is conceptualized using Turker's (2009) four-dimension, stakeholder-based scale — CSR toward social and non-social stakeholders, employees, customers, and government. Survey data were collected from 300 owners/managers of SMEs operating in Hanoi and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 3, with bootstrapping (5,000 resamples) and blindfolding procedures. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity (Cronbach's alpha 0.752-0.875; AVE 0.625 0.728; HTMT below 0.85), corroborated by exploratory factor analysis (KMO = 0.887; six factors, 67.03% variance explained). Results show that all four CSR dimensions positively and significantly influence REP (β = 0.133-0.298, p < 0.01), and REP in turn is the strongest predictor of FP (β = 0.469, p < 0.001), fully mediating the CSR-FP relationship as specified in the model. Firm size is the only significant control variable. CSR toward social/non-social stakeholders exerts the strongest effect, while CSR toward government exerts the weakest, a pattern explained through legitimacy theory as a "hygiene-factor" effect. The study contributes cross-cultural validation of Turker's scale in an emerging-economy SME context and offers evidence-based, prioritized managerial recommendations for CSR investment under resource constraints.

title: Green strategic orientations and enterprise performance in SMEs: The mediating role of green innovation
summary: This study examines how green strategic orientations contribute to enterprise performance (EP) in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) under increasing environmental and market pressures. Drawing on the natural resource-based view (NRBV) and recent evidence on green innovation (GI) and sustainable performance in SMEs (Liu et al., 2024), it distinguishes between green market orientation (GMO) and green learning orientation (GLO) and investigates their roles in driving GI. Using survey data from 415 Chinese manufacturing SMEs, structural equation modeling with bootstrap analysis is employed to test the proposed relationships. The results show that both GMO and GLO have significant positive effects on GI and EP. GI serves as a partial mediating mechanism linking strategic orientations to performance. Notably, GMO exerts a stronger influence on GI than GLO. These findings suggest that market-driven green strategies provide more immediate triggers for innovation, whereas learning-driven strategies support longer-term capability development. Overall, the results indicate that, under resource constraints, SMEs may achieve faster performance gains through externally oriented green strategies. The study provides practical insights for SME managers in prioritizing green strategic investments and aligning strategic orientation with innovation efforts to enhance performance, thereby contributing to the emerging literature on GLO and sustainable EP in SMEs (Rehman et al., 2024).

title: The Role of Green Finance in Promoting Sustainable Business Practices in India: A Conceptual framework
summary: Abstract Green finance has emerged as a critical mechanism for aligning capital allocation with environmental sustainability goals in India. This study examines how instruments such as green bonds, green loans, sustainability-linked finance, and related regulatory frameworks enable Indian businesses to adopt sustainable practices. This study also indicates that small-scale business organizations face limitations in accessing and benefiting from green finance due to inadequate awareness of the available regulatory frameworks, financial instruments, and related opportunities. The awareness of green finance has not yet reached the desired level within the business environment, which limits its effective adoption among small businesses.

title: Sailing on trust: The impact of social credit system construction on corporate ESG performance
summary: China’s construction of the social credit system (CSCS) is a significant measure for improving the basic market economy system and promoting sustainable economic development. With data from Chinese A-share listed enterprises spanning 2006–2024, this study considers the creation of CSCS demonstration pilot cities as a quasi-natural experiment, and analyzes its effects on corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance employing the difference-in-differences approach. The findings demonstrate that the CSCS has a significant promotional effect on ESG performance, and this conclusion remains valid following a number of robustness tests. Mechanism analysis reveals that the CSCS promotes enterprises’ ESG performance by alleviating financing constraints, reducing agency costs, and increasing public attention. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the CSCS improves the ESG performance of state-owned enterprises, firms with myopic managers, and those operating in less competitive industries more significantly. Additional investigation reveals that enterprises with lower ESG performance benefit more from the CSCS’s favorable effects on corporate ESG performance. Green finance reforms, financial supervision, information disclosure mechanisms, and digital economic development positively moderate the relationship between CSCS and corporate ESG performance. Additionally, corporate “greenwashing” tactics can be curbed by the CSCS. The above conclusions not only enrich the relevant research on corporate ESG performance, but also provide policy insights for the government to promote the CSCS, which has important practical significance for promoting a country’s sustainable development.

title: IMPROVING THE DEPRECIATION, REVALUATION, AND FINANCIAL REPORTING OF PROPERTY, PLANT, AND EQUIPMENT
summary: This paper examines issues related to calculating depreciation for property, plant, and equipment (fixed assets), their revaluation, accounting for repair and maintenance costs, and the disclosure of these assets in financial statements. It highlights the practical importance of selecting a depreciation method that aligns with the pattern of economic benefit consumption, systematically organizing the revaluation process, and accurately determining the results of asset derecognition.

title: Islamic Law in the Age of Technology and Digital Economy: Reconstructing Epistemology, Addressing Regulatory Challenges, and Rethinking the Future of Contemporary Fiqh
summary: This study analyzes the transformation of Islamic law in digital ecosystems, identifies epistemological and regulatory challenges, and formulates an integrative framework for contemporary fiqh. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence, blockchain, smart contracts, sharia-compliant fintech, and crypto-assets have transformed economic transactions while exposing limitations in conventional Islamic legal responses to digital phenomena. Using a Systematic literature review with qualitative thematic synthesis, the study examines scholarly publications, fatwas and legal decisions, regulatory documents, and supporting academic literature. The findings show four interconnected developments: digital transactions alter the manifestation of ownership, consent, contractual execution, and responsibility; classical uṣūl al-fiqh remains essential but requires contextual reconstruction through maqāṣid al-sharīʿah and technology-sensitive analysis; regulatory lag, cross-border transactions, digital-asset uncertainty, and AI ethics create significant governance challenges; and future Islamic legal governance requires multidisciplinary and adaptive institutional coordination. The study proposes the Neo-Digital Islamic Legal Framework (NDILF), integrating classical jurisprudential foundations, maqāṣid-oriented evaluation, digital ethics, and adaptive regulation through an iterative process of technological identification, multidisciplinary analysis, fatwa formulation, regulatory translation, and social-impact assessment.

title: Pathogen genomic sequencing supply chains in sub-Saharan Africa: exploring the role of Communities of Practice
summary: Purpose Supply chains for pathogen genomic sequencing (PGS) materials in sub-Saharan Africa face numerous noteworthy challenges that have received limited attention in research. This paper aims to highlight the most salient challenges from the perspective of key stakeholders in the supply chain and proposes a path toward sustainable solutions. Design/methodology/approach Using a qualitative approach, the authors conducted 54 extensive semi-structured interviews with stakeholders along the supply chain and used data analysis to highlight the key challenges. The authors then drew upon the literature and our analysis and experience to develop a set of design propositions for Communities of Practice (CoP) as locally-owned structures for knowledge sharing and learning on supply chain management (SCM) practices. Findings The authors identify nine categories of challenges, including long and unpredictable lead times, need for cold chain infrastructure and uncertain future funding. The authors also find evidence that stakeholders have siloed views of challenges which limits their ability to conceptualize sustainable solutions with long-term impact. Significant variability in the maturity of SCM practices between laboratories suggests the usefulness of a cross-organizational learning approach amongst laboratories, motivating the development of CoP. Originality/value PGS capacity in sub-Saharan Africa is at an early stage of development with multiple initiatives that are seeking to establish broad, equitable access. This paper provides a way forward for such initiatives by taking a comprehensive view of these supply chains and defining a number of design propositions for establishing CoP. The authors argue that improving labs’ SCM capabilities could have positive spillovers for the entire supply chain.

title: Artificial Intelligence in ESG and Financial Reporting
summary: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming an enabling technology for the collection, validation, analysis and communication of environmental, social and governance (ESG) information and financial information. At the same time, expanding sustainability disclosure requirements are increasing the volume, variety and frequency of non-financial information that organisations must manage. This paper examines how AI can strengthen the relationship between ESG reporting and financial reporting by improving data processing, anomaly detection, disclosure preparation, forecasting, risk identification and digital reporting. The study uses a qualitative, descriptive and exploratory research design based on secondary sources, including international reporting standards, Indian regulatory publications and recent academic literature. Particular attention is given to IFRS S1, IFRS S2, the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy, India's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) framework and BRSR Core. The findings indicate that AI can improve reporting timeliness, consistency, scalability and decision usefulness, but its effectiveness depends on data quality, governance, explainability, human oversight, cybersecurity and clear accountability. AI should therefore be treated as a controlled reporting technology rather than an autonomous substitute for professional judgement. The paper recommends an integrated AI-enabled reporting architecture with strong data lineage, model governance, human review, assurance controls and ethical safeguards.

title: AN EXPLORATIVE STUDY ON ENTREPRENEURSHIP SKILLS NEEDED BY ND/HND ACCOUNTANCY STUDENTS OF WAZIRI UMARU FEDERAL POLYTECHNIC BIRNIN KEBBI FOR SELF-EMPLOYMENT IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: This study investigated entrepreneurship skills needed by ND/HND Accountancy students of Waziri Umaru Federal Polytechnic Birnin Kebbi for self-employment in the digital economy. The study adopted descriptive survey design, guided by two research questions and one null hypothesis tested at 0.05 significance level. The population was 385 ND/HND Accountancy students (2024/2025 session), with a sample of 195 selected via Taro Yamane formula and stratified random sampling. The instrument (ESNSEQ) with 18 items on a 4-point scale was validated by three experts and yielded Cronbach Alpha of 0.86. 188 copies (96%) were retrieved and analyzed using mean, SD and independent samples t-test. Findings revealed accounting-related skills (cluster M=3.41) such as use of accounting software (M=3.62), bookkeeping for SMEs (M=3.61), business plan with financial projections (M=3.56), and POS accounting (M=3.55) are highly needed. General business management skills (cluster M=3.39) such as digital financial literacy (M=3.59), business plan writing (M=3.56) and ethical practices (M=3.47) were also highly needed. Hypothesis test showed no significant difference between ND (M=3.43) and HND (M=3.38) students (t=0.67, df=186, p=0.504). It was recommended that Accountancy curriculum should integrate QuickBooks, tax clinics and SME accounting practicum.

title: Toward Climate Change Resilience and the Carbon‐Neutral Transition in Emerging Economies Through Circular Technologies and Green Energy Transmission Systems
summary: ABSTRACT Despite growing evidence on the environmental benefits of green innovation, empirical findings for emerging economies remain limited and inconclusive, particularly regarding the joint role of environmental patents and renewable energy in reducing carbon emissions. Given the rapid economic growth of these countries, it is important to understand how environmental patents and climate change mitigation technologies influence sustainable economic growth in emerging markets. Using robust heterogeneous panel estimation methods that account for cross‐sectional dependence, the results consistently show that green innovation, measured by environmental patents, and renewable energy support the carbon‐neutral transition by reducing carbon emissions in emerging economies. The findings demonstrate that while green innovations significantly reduce emissions, the emissions‐reducing impact of renewable energy adoption is quantitatively larger. In contrast, energy consumption remains an important contributor to emissions. Overall, the study highlights that promoting green innovation together with renewable energy adoption is important for supporting long‐term environmental sustainability and the transition to carbon neutrality in emerging economies.

title: Impacts of the digital economy on industrial employment and CO2 emissions: a comparison between developed and developing countries
summary: This article assesses the impact of the digital economy on industry and the environment by comparing 15 countries (7 developed and 8 developing) over the period 2000–2021. Using the System Generalized Method of Moments (SYS-GMM), the analysis reveals contrasting results between country groups. For developed countries, a 1% increase in ICT imports is associated with a 0.159% reduction in CO₂ emissions (p-value < 0.01) and a marginal 0.038% decrease in industrial employment (p-value < 0.10), consistent with automation-driven labor reallocation toward high-value-added sectors. In developing countries, the same 1% increase in ICT imports yields an insignificant effect on CO₂ emissions (− 0.008, p-value = 0.676) and industrial employment (− 0.016, p-value = 0.113), reflecting structural constraints including outdated energy infrastructure and limited absorptive capacity for green technologies. Industrial value-added positively influences employment in both groups, though the elasticity is higher in developed economies (0.048 vs. 0.031). The results underscore the need for developed countries to sustain investments in advanced digital infrastructure and innovation policies that accelerate the green digital transition. For developing countries, priorities should include strengthening green digital infrastructure, fostering international technology-transfer partnerships, and implementing targeted workforce retraining programs to maximize the employment and environmental co-benefits of digitalization.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility, Firm Size, And Tax Aggressiveness in LQ45 Companies
summary: The relationship between corporate social responsibility disclosure, firm size, and tax aggressiveness is examined among companies included in the LQ45 index of the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2024. Secondary data were obtained from audited financial statements, annual reports, and sustainability reports. Purposive sampling produced 25 companies that remained consistently listed and reported profits throughout the observation period, yielding 100 firm-year observations. Tax aggressiveness was represented by the effective tax rate, corporate social responsibility was measured through a 30-item Annexure-A disclosure index, and firm size was calculated using the natural logarithm of total assets. Multiple linear regression was performed with SPSS version 26 after tests of normality, multicollinearity, heteroscedasticity, and autocorrelation. Corporate social responsibility produced a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient toward the effective tax rate, while firm size also produced a positive and insignificant coefficient. The simultaneous test confirmed that both predictors failed to explain tax aggressiveness significantly, with an adjusted coefficient of determination of only 0.3 percent. Intensive social disclosure and substantial asset capacity therefore do not automatically determine the tax behavior of highly visible and liquid firms. The contribution lies in demonstrating the limited explanatory power of disclosure intensity and asset scale within the institutional setting of LQ45 companies

title: Determinants of ESG-Related Digital Transparency: Evidence from Energy Firms in Emerging Economies
summary: Existing research has largely treated digital transformation and ESG performance as separate dimensions, while widely used ESG indicators are strongly driven by disclosure practices. This creates a measurement problem, as it remains unclear how companies’ underlying sustainability performance translates into effective digital transparency. This study addresses this gap by analyzing the relationship between ESG performance and ESG-related digital transparency, defined as companies’ capacity to disclose sustainability-related information through digital systems. We construct a novel ESG-Related Digital Transparency Index (EDTI), capturing key dimensions of disclosure, compliance, and firm capacity through a composite structure based on principal component analysis, in which the largest contribution is associated with the Digital Governance and Transparency sub-index. Using an unbalanced panel of 95 energy firms (2015–2024), based on annual data, and a dynamic panel model, the results show that digital transparency is highly persistent and positively associated with adjusted ESG performance. Environmental policies reinforce this relationship, while financial factors play a more limited role. Moreover, ESG performance amplifies the effect of environmental pressures, highlighting the role of interaction mechanisms. These findings show how substantive ESG capabilities translate into digital transparency, emphasizing the role of organizational and informational processes in firms’ sustainability-related digital development.

title: Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurial Resilience Among Small Businesses in Imo State Nigeria
summary: This study examined the effect of digital transformation on entrepreneurial resilience among small businesses in Imo State, Nigeria. Guided by three objectives, the study specifically explored the influence of digital adoption, digital innovation, and e-commerce integration on the ability of small enterprises to maintain business continuity, adapt to market changes, and sustain financial performance. The research employed a descriptive survey design, collecting primary data from 287 small business owners across Owerri, Orlu, and Okigwe using structured questionnaires. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. Findings revealed that digital transformation significantly enhances entrepreneurial resilience, with digital adoption showing the strongest effect, followed by digital innovation and e-commerce integration. The study concludes that small businesses that integrate technology, innovate digitally, and engage in online commerce are better equipped to withstand operational challenges, adapt to environmental changes, and maintain financial stability. Recommendations include prioritizing digital adoption, investing in digital innovation, leveraging e-commerce platforms, and receiving institutional support for digital capacity building. The study contributes to the literature by providing localized empirical evidence on the link between digital transformation and resilience, offering insights for entrepreneurs, policymakers, and SME support organizations in Imo State.

title: Governance Through Decision-Making Structure: a Driver of Corporate Social Responsibility in Cameroonian SMEs
summary: Abstract This article examines the influence of decision-making structure, understood as a formal mechanism of internal governance, on the social and societal practices of Cameroonian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Drawing on stakeholder theory and resource dependence theory, the study posits that a more open, participative and diversified decision-making structure fosters responsible engagement toward employees and the local community. Data were collected through a questionnaire administered to fifty-two SME managers in the city of Douala and processed with SPSS (principal component analysis, Cronbach's alpha, simple linear regression). Results show that decision-making structure positively and significantly explains the social and societal practices of the SMEs studied (standardized beta of 0.735; R² of 0.541; F of 58.815; p < .001). These findings confirm the research hypothesis and are consistent with prior studies conducted in Cameroonian and African contexts. The article discusses these results in light of the existing literature and proposes managerial implications relating to the participation of middle managers and women in decision-making bodies, and to the delegation of managerial responsibilities within SMEs. Keywords: decision-making structure, corporate governance, corporate social responsibility, SMEs, stakeholders, Cameroon.

title: Industrial digitalization: a continuous input-output accounting framework and evidence from China
summary: The rapid development of the digital economy has shifted attention from expanding digital industries towards the integration of digital technologies into traditional production systems. However, existing measures based on digital industry scale, proxy indicators, or composite indices may not adequately capture the structural penetration of digital technologies across inter-industry production networks. To address this limitation, this study develops an input-output accounting framework integrating RAS-based structural updating, digital input identification, and value-added decomposition. Using this framework, we construct a provincial input-output dataset for 30 Chinese provinces from 2007 to 2022 and measure the scale and evolution of industrial digitalization. The results show sustained expansion and structural embedding of digital technologies in China’s production system. The tertiary sector exhibits the highest level and fastest growth, followed by the secondary sector, while the primary sector remains less digitalized. Spatially, regional concentration coexists with broader diffusion: advanced provinces remain leaders, while cross-provincial disparities gradually narrow. These findings highlight the cumulative, network-based nature of industrial digitalization and demonstrate the value of continuous input-output accounting for capturing its temporal, sectoral, and regional dynamics. The framework provides a consistent measurement infrastructure for data-constrained environments. The results reflect structural penetration and dynamic evolution rather than causal effects.

title: Does Good Governance Make CEO Communications More Realistic?
summary: ABSTRACT In corporate communications, the frequent use of positive words is commonly associated with impression management, while negative words are often considered to have higher informational value, an effect known as the informational negativity effect. This study examines whether corporate governance performance is associated with the frequency of positive and negative words. The study adopts a multidisciplinary approach that draws from social psychology, impression management, and corporate governance research. Examining corporate governance scores and CEO communications for 75 firms on the FTSE 100 index reveals that governance performance is negatively associated with positive words and positively associated with negative words. These findings support the view that strong internal governance mechanisms reduce the incidence of impression management by limiting the use of positive words while enhancing the informative elements. This also aligns with the board's ethical responsibility for the corporation's communication strategy, ensuring that its communications with shareholders and other stakeholders provide a true and fair view.

title: Balancing risk and opportunity: Digital transformation, cybersecurity investments, and export performance in low-tech firms
summary: This study examines whether investments in digital technologies raise export sales among low-tech firms, and whether cybersecurity spending conditions these returns. Reading the Resource-Based View through resource orchestration, we frame digital technologies as enabling resources and cybersecurity as a protective commitment securing their value but competing for the investment budget under scarcity. This competition is sharper in low-tech firms, with thinner slack. Using Bank of Italy data (2016–2023), we find digital investment positively associated with export sales where cybersecurity spending is absent. This association is negative in the highest protective-spending brackets, and a specification imposing no functional form locates the reversal at the top of the distribution. The pattern is clearer among SMEs and manufacturing firms; among larger firms, digital investment shows no association with exports, while protective spending is associated with higher export volume. This is a cyber-risk paradox: under scarcity, protection substitutes for, rather than complements, digital expansion.

title: Digital Transformation and Performance of Human Resource Function in State Corporations in Nairobi County, Kenya.
summary: Digital transformation, the integration of digital technologies into organizational processes to enhance efficiency, innovation and value creation, is increasingly repositioning the human resource (HR) function from an administrative unit into a strategic driver of organizational performance. In Kenya, state corporations have progressively adopted human resource information systems (HRIS) and e-HRM platforms to enhance accountability and service delivery; however, over 30% of public institutions still experience inefficiencies in HR processes such as delayed recruitment, payroll errors and low productivity, while less than 40% utilize HR analytics effectively. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to establish the influence of digital transformation on the performance of the HR function in state corporations in Nairobi County, Kenya. It specifically examined the influence of strategic leadership, HR technology ecosystem, data analytics infrastructure and workforce digital literacy on the performance of the HR function. The study was anchored on the Transformational Leadership Theory, the Resource-Based View, the Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Technology Acceptance Model. A descriptive correlational research design was adopted, targeting 170 state corporations headquartered in Nairobi County, from which a sample of 119 was determined using Nassiuma's formula and selected through stratified random sampling, with HR managers, HR officers and administrative staff involved in HR operations as respondents. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered online. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods, namely Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis, were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four digital transformation dimensions jointly explained 48.9% of the variation in the performance of the HR function (F = 15.5063, p < 0.05). The HR technology ecosystem had the strongest positive and significant influence on HR function performance, followed by data analytics infrastructure and strategic leadership, while workforce digital literacy had a positive and significant but comparatively weaker influence. The study, therefore, recommends that state corporations should strengthen strategic leadership by improving vision clarity, communication of digital transformation goals and resource allocation; upgrade and fully integrate HR systems tailored to institutional needs; strengthen HR analytics capability, data quality governance and system integration; and intensify continuous digital skills development focused on employee confidence, advanced system proficiency and consistent technology adoption.

title: FinTech et transformation du secteur bancaire dans les économies émergentes : une analyse bibliométrique
summary: Cette étude analyse le rôle des technologies financières dans la transformation du secteur bancaire des économies émergentes à travers une approche bibliométrique. À partir d’un corpus de 130 articles scientifiques extraits de la base Scopus sur la période 2015–2025, la recherche combine une analyse descriptive et une analyse de réseaux réalisée à l’aide du logiciel VOSviewer. L’objectif est d’identifier les tendances de la production scientifique, les principales thématiques de recherche, les structures intellectuelles et les dynamiques de collaboration dans ce champ en expansion. Les résultats montrent une croissance significative des publications, particulièrement après 2020, traduisant un intérêt académique croissant pour la FinTech dans le contexte de la transformation digitale des systèmes financiers. L’analyse de co-occurrence des mots-clés met en évidence la centralité des concepts de FinTech, d’inclusion financière et de finance digitale. Les analyses de couplage bibliographique et de clustering indiquent que la littérature s’organise autour de trois axes principaux : la digitalisation du secteur bancaire, l’inclusion financière dans les économies émergentes et l’innovation financière. Toutefois, les réseaux de co-auteurs et de collaboration institutionnelle demeurent fragmentés, suggérant une faible intégration des communautés scientifiques. L’étude contribue ainsi à une meilleure compréhension de la structuration scientifique du champ et suggère des pistes de recherche encore insuffisamment explorées, notamment en matière de régulation, de gouvernance et de stabilité financière.

title: AI-DRIVEN DECISION SUPPORT FOR SME DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND FINANCIAL RESILIENCE: EVIDENCE FROM EAST JAVA, INDONESIA
summary: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) play a crucial role in supporting regional economic growth; however, many SMEs continue to face challenges in digital transformation, data-driven decision-making, and financial management. This study aims to analyze SME digital transformation readiness, identify financial management challenges, and develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven decision support platform called SENTRA-AI (Smart Enterprise Analytics) to enhance financial resilience and business competitiveness. The study employed a mixed-method approach with a sequential explanatory design, integrating quantitative surveys, qualitative interviews, observations, and Design Science Research (DSR) for system development. The findings indicate that most SMEs have adopted basic digital technologies but remain limited in utilizing business analytics, financial intelligence, and AI-based decision-support tools. The implementation of SENTRA-AI improved financial monitoring, sales forecasting, operational efficiency, and digital capability among SME owners. This study contributes by providing an AI-enabled decision-support artifact that supports digital transformation and financial resilience within the context of emerging economy SMEs.

title: Digital transformation indicators for green transition: Spatial spillovers, innovation pathways, and regime heterogeneity in Vietnam
summary: Digital transformation is increasingly treated as enabling infrastructure for sustainability transitions, yet regional indicator systems rarely capture its multidimensional and spatial character. This study develops a five-dimensional Digital Transformation Indicator (DTI) and examines its association with energy efficiency and green total factor productivity across 63 Vietnamese provinces during 2010-2023. The empirical framework combines principal component analysis, two-way fixed effects, Spatial Durbin Models, threshold estimation, and mechanism-consistent pathway analysis. Digital capability is positively associated with both green-transition outcomes. Spatial decomposition indicates that 37.5% of the total DTI-energy-efficiency association is indirect, consistent with cross-provincial spillovers. For the innovation pathway, the sample product-of-coefficients estimate is 0.127 (38.2% of the total association), while the mean of the bootstrap distribution is 0.144 (95% CI: 0.089-0.212), implying an indicative mechanism-consistent share of about 38-43%. A single digital-capability regime threshold is identified at DTI = 0.487 (95% CI: 0.441-0.531), above which the marginal association more than doubles. Results remain stable across alternative index constructions, spatial weights, temporal specifications, and falsification checks. Because the design is observational, all estimates are interpreted as conditional spatial associations rather than causal effects. The study contributes a diagnostically assessed subnational indicator framework and evidence relevant to coordinated digital-green investment and region-specific capability building in emerging economies.

title: Disentangling large-scale supply networks: f-HiCoNE framework for flow-hierarchical clustering via combinatorial Hodge decomposition
summary: Abstract Modern society relies on complex supply chains to sustain the flow of goods and services that are essential to daily life. While traditional supply chain theory assumes a clear, hierarchical flow from upstream suppliers to downstream customers, observable real-world transaction networks rarely exhibit this acyclic structure. Instead, detailed inter-firm data reveal that interwoven networks are heavily entangled by cyclic flows. Consequently, without appropriate partitioning of these massive inter-firm networks, the latent flow-hierarchical structures that are central to supply chain concepts remain obscure. To address this analytical challenge, we introduce the flow-Hierarchical Community Network Extraction (f-HiCoNE) framework. By applying combinatorial Hodge decomposition, this approach disentangles the complex inter-firm network by isolating the acyclic gradient flow to quantify the flow-hierarchical parts and partition the graph. By applying f-HiCoNE to a nationwide transaction dataset of approximately 650,000 firms, we extracted clusters exhibiting the flow-hierarchical organisation that supply-chain theory assumes. These clusters demonstrated strong flow-hierarchical organisation, wherein the upstream-downstream positioning of firms was well described by local scalar potentials, revealing distinct geographically localised industrial ecosystems. This study provides a map that could help firms understand their surrounding environment and locate their position within an inter-firm network and opens a new research avenue focused on flow-hierarchy clustering in supply chain analysis.

title: Urban heat as a structural development challenge in rapidly growing cities
summary: Urban heat is increasingly emerging as a major constraint on sustainable development, particularly in rapidly growing cities of the Global South. Although urban heat is commonly addressed through local adaptation and urban heat reduction measures such as urban greening, cool and super cool roofs, and building retrofits or passive design, these interventions are increasingly implemented against a backdrop of accelerating planetary warming, fiscal constraints, and persistent socio-economic inequalities. This Essay argues that urban heat should be understood not merely as an environmental, technological, or urban planning challenge, but as a structural development problem arising from the interaction of climate change, rapid urbanization, uneven governance capacity, and political-economic processes that shape vulnerability and adaptive capacity. Drawing on evidence from urban climate, adaptation, development, and climate justice literatures, we examine how escalating heat risks intersect with infrastructure deficits, debt burdens, limited access to climate finance, and unequal access to cooling resources across rapidly growing cities. We show that climate change mitigation and local action, including urban heat reduction and broader adaptation measures, perform distinct but complementary functions, and that local interventions alone cannot overcome the broader climatic and structural conditions that increasingly constrain their effectiveness and scalability. Urban heat risks are further amplified by profound inequalities in exposure, vulnerability, and access to adaptation resources, creating a widening mismatch between those facing the greatest heat burdens and those possessing the greatest capacity to respond. We, therefore, argue that effective urban heat governance requires moving beyond predominantly local and technocratic approaches toward integrated strategies that combine climate change mitigation, equitable climate finance, enhanced fiscal capacity, and multi-level governance. Reframing urban heat as a structural development challenge provides a more comprehensive framework for addressing climate justice, resilience, and long-term urban habitability under a warming climate.

title: Smart governance and its role in achieving digital transformation requirements: A survey study in selected Iraqi universities
summary: Background With modern technology ever more entrenched in tertiary schooling, digital change has become an urgent necessity to enhance both the educational and administrative processes within universities. Anbar, Fallujah, and Maarif Universities now aim to adopt digital transformation strategies to improve academic and administrative efficiency while developing services provided to students and faculty. Within this framework, savvy governance plays a pivotal role in ensuring the application of principles like transparency, accountability, and participation, which are core factors for boosting the effectiveness of digital change. Literature indicates that integrating smart governance practices into higher education institutions contributes to achieving a modern and flexible educational environment with the dexterity to keep pace with technological progress. Methodology The research followed a descriptive and analytical approach. The method used was a questionnaire administered to a sample of 83 employees in positions (dean, assistant dean, department head) at the universities under study (Anbar University, Fallujah University, and Al-Maarif University). The study will be conducted over the period from April 7, 2025, to September 1, 2025. Results The descriptive results reveal that the university has consistently adopted smart governance tools, particularly the efficient use of the dimensions of transparency, participation, accountability, collaboration, and innovation, which have contributed to the universities’ transformation into a digital system. The study also demonstrated a high positive correlation of 0.93 between smart governance and digital transformation in the universities in the study area, confirming the close relationship between the studied variables. Conclusions Integrating smart governance with digital transformation plays a pivotal role in enhancing institutional efficiency by promoting transparency, accountability, and innovation. This contributes to improving service quality, increasing beneficiary satisfaction, and supporting sustainable development.

title: ESG PERFORMANCE AND PROFITABILITY IN VIETNAMESE AGRICULTURAL FIRMS: PANEL AND PREDICTIVE EVIDENCE
summary: Whether environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investment improves firm profitability remains uncertain in agriculture, where sustainability initiatives may reduce operating risks but require substantial up-front costs. This study examines the relationship between ESG performance and return on assets (ROA) using an unbalanced panel of 683 firm-year observations from 78 Vietnamese agricultural firms during 2016–2025. Firm and year fixed-effects models are employed, supplemented by lagged specifications, production-system comparisons, and a limited predictive analysis using Elastic Net and Random Forest. The results show that aggregate ESG performance is not significantly associated with profitability, while governance exhibits a positive relationship with ROA. The financial relevance of ESG also varies across production systems, with stronger effects observed among livestock firms and differences in the environmental dimension between livestock and crop production. Predictive improvements from nonlinear machine-learning models are limited. Overall, the findings suggest that ESG–profitability relationships in agriculture are primarily pillar- and production-specific rather than reflecting a uniform ESG premium.

title: Digital Transformation Through Online Shopping: Assessing Its Contribution To Green Technology Adoption And Sustainable Consumption
summary: Digital transformation has significantly reshaped consumer behaviour and created new opportunities for promoting sustainable consumption. This study examines the relationship between Online Shopping Digitalisation (OSD), Green Technology Adoption (GTA), and Sustainable Consumption (SC) among online consumers. The study aims to assess the relationships among these constructs and examine the potential mediating role of GTA in the relationship between OSD and SC. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 220 online consumers using a structured questionnaire and five-point Likert scale. Data were analysed using SPSS through descriptive statistics, correlation, and regression analysis, while PLS-SEM is proposed for further assessment of the measurement and structural models. The findings indicate significant positive relationships between OSD and GTA (β = .261, p < .001), OSD and SC (β = .299, p < .001), and GTA and SC (β = .465, p < .001). The study highlights the importance of integrating digitalisation and green technology to promote sustainable consumption.
