title: Digital transformation and sustainable competitive advantage in SMEs: unpacking the mediating role of absorptive capacity in emerging economies
summary: Despite the growing recognition of digital transformation as a driver of sustainable competitive advantage, empirical evidence from small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in developing economies remains limited. This study examines the mediating role of absorptive capacity in the relationship between digital transformation and sustainable competitive advantage among SMEs in Southern Ethiopia. Drawing on the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, and Absorptive Capacity Theory, the study employed an explanatory cross-sectional design using data collected from 267 SME owners and managers through stratified random sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that digital transformation significantly enhances sustainable competitive advantage both directly and indirectly through absorptive capacity, indicating a complementary mediation effect. The study contributes to the literature by integrating three complementary theoretical perspectives to explain how digital transformation creates sustainable competitive advantage in resource-constrained SMEs. The findings further suggest that SMEs should complement digital investments with strong knowledge acquisition, assimilation, and application capabilities to sustain long-term competitiveness.

title: BHDSF v2 - Benghazi Human Digital Safety Framework: Foundations of Human Security in the Digital Transformation Era
summary: This record adds BHDSF Phase II field instrument to Phase I framework (Zenodo, June 2026). Phase I measured 100 students at Shabab Al-Intifada School, Benghazi, showing 48% exposed to digital threats and phishing detection increase from 31% to 81% after gamified intervention. A key gap was exclusion of parents, despite reporting chain "Tell Mom and Dad". Phase II design: cross-sectional paper survey of n=200 parents/guardians (100 paired to Phase I students via code P-S-NN ↔ S01-P01, and 100 expansion sample). Non-probability purposive sampling. Tool: 20 items in 4 sections (A: phishing/domain analysis Q1-5, B: password hygiene Q6-10, C: privacy/apps/AI exposure Q11-16, D: incident response/trust Q17-20). 17 scored points + 3 qualitative. Arabic with Libyan dialect open questions. Anonymized linking, no names/photos. Planned analysis: descriptive, paired gap indicator (Parent - Student), correlation, Holm correction, thematic coding. Status: Fieldwork not completed at time of writing; this file is the design paper and survey instrument. It provides, to authors' knowledge, the first paired parent-child cybersecurity dataset design in post-conflict Libya, aligned with UNICEF/ITU Child Online Protection guidelines. title: Beyond Physical Destruction: Typhoon Shocks, Innovation Retrenchment, and the Limits of Adaptive Capacity
summary: ABSTRACT Using a comprehensive panel of Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2003 to 2024, this study investigates the causal impact of typhoon shocks on innovation performance and the heterogeneity of adaptive strategies. We find that typhoon shocks significantly suppress firms' innovation output by crowding out resources available for R&D and heightening perceptions of operational and managerial uncertainty. Our analysis of adaptive capacity reveals that while hardware‐based automation (industrial robots), government subsidies, and less competitive industry environments buffer the shock, artificial intelligence (AI) has yet to demonstrate significant resilience benefits. Furthermore, we identify a negative spillover effect where climate risks propagate through supply chain networks, amplifying vulnerabilities for downstream firms. These findings highlight the critical role of physical infrastructure resilience and supply chain coordination in sustaining long‐term competitiveness.

title: Ethnic diversity and its effect on audit lag
summary: This study investigates the effects of chief executive officer (CEO) ethnicity, audit committee ethnic diversity, audit tenure, and accounting financial expertise on audit delay in consumer non-cyclical (CNC) companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). Drawing upon the resource-based view (Barney, 1991) and expanding the demographic frameworks of prior literature (Harjoto et al., 2015), this research employs a quantitative methodology using panel data regression with a fixed-effect model (FEM) on 73 firms during the 2022–2023 period (146 firm-year observations). The empirical results reveal that CEO ethnicity, audit committee ethnic diversity, and accounting financial expertise are significantly and negatively associated with audit delay, effectively minimizing financial reporting lag. Conversely, audit tenure exerts a significant positive influence on audit delay, suggesting that prolonged auditor-client relationships may compromise independence and slow reporting. These findings offer critical practical insights for companies, regulators, and investors aiming to strengthen internal corporate governance mechanisms and optimize financial reporting efficiency in emerging markets. Future studies can extend this single-sector scope by investigating broader governance determinants across diverse industries.

title: Securing the oligonucleotide supply chain: addressing raw material risks, environmental pressures, and geopolitical factors
summary: The rapid growth of the oligonucleotide therapeutics field has highlighted how vulnerable the supporting supply chain can be. As the demand increases, manufacturers must face constraints in raw materials, increasing environmental pressures, and a shifting geopolitical landscape. Companies must adopt strategic measures to ensure an adequate supply of raw materials. Nucleic Acid Insights brought together a panel of experts to discuss the key challenges and emerging solutions in this space. The discussion covers how the industry can build supply chain resilience, mitigate risk, and create sustainable supply networks for oligonucleotide therapeutics.

title: Do ESG Commitments Curb Tax Avoidance? Evidence from ASEAN Banks and the Moderating Role of Audit Quality
summary: This study investigates the performance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and earnings management (loan loss provisions) on tax avoidance measured using Effective Tax Rate (ETR) and Cash Effective Tax Rate (CETR) with audit quality as a moderator in the banking sector in ASEAN. Using panel data regression analysis and moderated regression analysis matching 101 banks with 707 bank-year observations, empirical results show that ESG performance has an adverse effect on tax avoidance, meaning that a high ESG score can reduce the potential for tax avoidance. Earnings management is positively associated with tax avoidance, especially when measured by ETR. Another important finding is the role of audit quality, which is driven by the involvement of the big four auditors, as a significant moderation variable. Audit quality reinforces the negative relationship between ESG and tax avoidance and weakens the positive relationship between Discretionary Loan Loss Provisions (DLLP) and tax avoidance. These results confirm the importance of external audit supervision in suppressing aggressive tax strategies. This research contributes to developing agency theory and legitimacy by showing how high-quality audits can drive ethical financial practices. Practically, this study recommends strengthening the role of professional auditors and integrating ESG indicators and audit quality in evaluating corporate tax behavior.

title: Evaluation of Indonesia’s Legal and Institutional Framework for Environmental Pollution Mitigation
summary: Environmental pollution is a major challenge to Indonesia’s environmental governance, despite its relatively comprehensive legal framework, due to pressures from urbanization, industrialization, mining, waste, air pollution, and deforestation. This study examines the effectiveness of Indonesia’s legal and institutional framework in addressing environmental pollution through comparison with the legal systems of Uganda and East Africa. The study employs a normative legal method with statutory and comparative approaches to Uganda, particularly the National Environment Management Authority (NEMA). This study demonstrates, first, Law No. 6 of 2023 potentially weakens environmental protection through the centralization of EIA, restrictions on public access, reduced recognition of local wisdom, and uncertainty regarding strict liability. Second, institutional changes under Law No. 6 of 2023 create ambiguity in the division of authority and coordination of environmental oversight between central and regional governments, potentially creating gaps in oversight and accountability. Third, based on comparison with Uganda, this study recommends strengthening risk-based EIA, access to information and public participation, pollution control, strict liability, and integrated environmental oversight and enforcement oriented towards environmental restoration. Thus, the study aims to strengthen Indonesia’s environmental governance towards ecologically just pollution control

title: Conceptualizing Sustainable Media: An Integrated Model for Environmental Journalism in Iran
summary: The climate crisis and environmental degradation have intensified ecological, social, and economic challenges in Iran, increasing the need for environmental communication that supports public engagement, policy development, and long-term environmental governance. However, environmental reporting remains largely episodic and constrained by political, legal, organizational, and professional limitations. This study develops an empirically grounded conceptual model of sustainable media using a grounded theory approach based on interviews with Iranian journalists, media managers, documentary filmmakers, communication scholars, and environmental experts. The findings conceptualize sustainable media as a model comprising causal, contextual, intervening, strategic, and consequential components. The model proposes that sustainable media can be maintained through the interaction of institutional capacities, including legal protection, economic independence, organizational resilience, scientific expertise, and professional development, with communicative capacities such as agenda-setting, audience orientation, transparency, editorial independence, and collaboration among journalists, scientists, and environmental stakeholders. These capacities support continuous, context-sensitive, and solution-oriented environmental journalism. The study contributes to environmental communication scholarship by integrating perspectives on environmental communication, mediatization, and hybrid media systems into a unified framework in a West Asian context and offers practical insights for strengthening environmental journalism and long-term environmental governance in an ecologically vulnerable and politically constrained environment.

title: The Effect of Audit Quality, Tenure Audit, And Auditor Reputation On Fraudulent Financial Reporting with Institutional Ownership As A Moderation Variable in Industrial Companies Listed on the IDX For The 2021-2025 Period
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of audit quality, audit tenure, and auditor reputation on fraudulent financial reporting, with institutional ownership as a moderating variable in industrial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2021–2025. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data from audited financial statements and annual reports. The population consists of all industrial sector companies listed on the IDX, and purposive sampling yielded 49 companies or 245 firm-year observations. Fraudulent financial reporting is measured using the Beneish M-Score, audit quality is proxied by the natural logarithm of audit fees, audit tenure is measured by the length of the auditor-client engagement, auditor reputation is measured by a Big Four dummy variable, and institutional ownership is measured by the percentage of shares held by institutional investors. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA), with model selection through the Chow Test and Hausman Test. The results show that audit quality has a significant negative effect on fraudulent financial reporting (β = -0.284, p < 0.001); audit tenure has a significant positive effect (β = 0.157, p < 0.01); auditor reputation has a significant negative effect (β = -0.312, p < 0.001); and institutional ownership significantly strengthens the negative effect of audit quality (interaction β = -0.146, p < 0.01) and weakens the positive effect of audit tenure on fraudulent financial reporting (interaction β = -0.119, p < 0.05). These findings indicate that audit quality and auditor reputation are important mechanisms for detecting and preventing fraudulent financial reporting, and this role is strengthened by the presence of institutional ownership as an external monitoring mechanism

title: Sustainability Accounting in the 21st Century Economy
summary: This study explores literature survey approach with content search analysis on existing reports, research papers and publications bordering on Sustainability Accounting and the theoretical foundations and applications of Sustainability Accounting in modern economic systems. Grounded in stakeholder theory, legitimacy theory, institutional theory and normative theory, the study underscores how Sustainability Accounting expands the scope of Traditional Accounting to include Environmental, Social, Governance and Economic (ESG-E) metrics. Reporting frameworks such as the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), and the European Union’s Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) illustrate the institutionalization of sustainability practices and reflect the growing demand for transparency and accountability. The study revealed that Sustainability Accounting is essential for promoting responsible business conduct and sustainable development and that for businesses to be relevant with greater market share, the non-financial reporting aspect (ESG report) should be taken seriously as it enhances the credibility, reliability and acceptability of the financial reporting aspect (Economic report) in the 21st century economy. As economies become more interdependent and sustainability risks intensify, the integration of nonfinancial reporting into mainstream accounting practices is not just beneficial, it is imperative. Thus, the study concludes that Sustainability Accounting advances accounting thought by recognizing the interconnectedness of environmental, social, governance and economic performance.

title: Impact of Data Analytics Adoption on Audit Quality in the Public Sector Accounting Reporting
summary: This study investigates the impact of data analytics adoption on audit quality within the context of public sector accounting reporting in Nigeria, focusing specifically on federal government owned tertiary institutions. Drawing on survey data from 98 audit professionals across 130 institutions, the research employs quantitative analysis, including T-tests, to evaluate the effects of data analytics on key dimensions of audit quality: timeliness of financial reporting, audit risk assessment, and resource allocation efficiency. The findings reveal that data analytics significantly enhances the timeliness and accuracy of financial statement reporting, improves the effectiveness of risk assessments, and optimizes resource allocation in audit processes. Despite these positive outcomes, challenges such as limited digital infrastructure and skill gaps among auditors persist. The study concludes that the adoption of data analytics in public sector accounting reporting significantly enhances audit quality by improving the timeliness of financial reporting, strengthening risk assessment, and optimizing resource allocation, thereby fostering greater transparency and accountability in Nigeria’s federal government-owned tertiary institutions. It is therefore, recommended that federal government owned tertiary institutions in Nigeria invest in continuous auditor training, robust technological infrastructure, and supportive regulatory frameworks to fully leverage data analytics for enhanced audit quality and improved public sector financial reporting.

title: Enhancing Nigerian Banks Governance: Any Role for Independent Directors?
summary: One essential component and the pinnacle of sound corporate governance is the selection of independent directors. They are essential in bank's board in order to prevent corporate scandals like the ones involving Worldcom and Eron, among others. Even before formal rules to that effect were introduced, codes in Nigeria emphasized the value of independent directors. However, the crucial question has been whether they contribute in any way to the advancement of sound corporate governance in banks. It is argued that the fact that banks and companies are now vying for independent directors is a clear indication of the value that these individuals bring to the banks. By providing the board of directors with independent and objective viewpoints, they are supposed to reflect the interests of minority shareholders and serve as a check on the banks' management. It is suggested that the teething issues of appointment process, industry experience, available time, and tenure on the board must be addressed immediately in order for the independent director to fulfill its duties to the banks.

title: Carbon Pricing and Green Finance in Road Transport: A Bibliometric Analysis of Low-Carbon Transition Mechanisms
summary: Abstract In the face of the escalating climate crisis, the decarbonization of road transport and the transition towards a low-carbon economy have become strategic priorities for governments, particularly given the transport sector’s significant contribution to global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. In this context, carbon pricing and green finance have emerged as two complementary policy instruments capable of accelerating the sector’s transformation. Carbon taxation seeks to internalize the environmental costs associated with GHG emissions within economic decision-making, while green finance aims to mobilize the financial resources required to support sustainable development, enhance energy efficiency, and promote the adoption of lower-carbon mobility solutions. Despite the growing body of research in both fields, their interplay within the specific context of road transport decarbonization remains relatively fragmented in the scientific literature. This study is based on a systematic review of the scientific literature, primarily using the Scopus database to gather relevant publications on carbon pricing, green finance, and road transport. Bibliometric tools, notably VOSviewer, were employed to analyze and visualize keyword co-occurrence networks, author collaborations, and citation linkages to map the interactions among core concepts. The objective is to identify research trends, major contributions, and scientific gaps concerning the role of carbon pricing and green finance mechanisms in driving the low-carbon transition of the transport sector. The findings highlight a steady rise in academic interest regarding how fiscal instruments and sustainable investments support transportation decarbonization. Additionally, keyword and co-author networks reveal distinct research clusters focused on environmental governance, green economics, and sustainable transport development. These results underscore the critical importance of carbon pricing and green finance as key catalysts for transforming road transport systems. Keywords: Carbon pricing, carbon tax, green finance, climate finance, road transport, decarbonization, sustainability.

title: Technology Push or Demand Pull? Supply-Chain AI Spillovers and the Quality of Green Innovation Toward Sustainable Production in Chinese Listed Firms
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) diffuses beyond adopting firms into the wider production network, yet the direction and quality of these spillovers remain underexplored, an omission that matters because only high-quality green innovation advances genuine sustainable transformation. We ask how supply-chain AI spillovers shape the citation-weighted quality of firms’ green patents and whether technology-push and demand-pull channels carry equal weight. Building inter-industry AI exposure from a pre-sample (2012) input–output structure for 4963 Chinese A-share listed firms over 2011 to 2023, and identifying effects with a shift-share instrument, we find that AI exposure significantly raises green innovation quality. Upstream technology-push spillovers dominate downstream demand-pull spillovers on average, but the asymmetry is conditional on supply-chain structure: the upstream channel prevails when suppliers are concentrated, and the downstream channel re-emerges when they are dispersed. The effect concentrates in green invention patents rather than utility models and operates through embedded technology transfer rather than in-house R&D. Sequencing AI toward upstream, input–output-dense sectors offers a network-level lever for steering digital technology toward high-quality green innovation and a more sustainable production system.

title: Habitar o rentar: La vivienda en España entre el derecho y el activo
summary: This article examines housing in Spain through the tension between its social function as a place to live and its economic role as an investment asset. Combining a social anthropological perspective with political economy, it discusses housing affordability, residential insecurity and the uneven distribution of opportunities to buy or rent. The analysis considers housing financialisation and the role of institutional investors alongside other factors, including household incomes, housing supply and tourist accommodation. It examines public housing provision, rent regulation and the distribution of responsibilities across national, regional and local government. Parliamentary negotiations and housing movements are discussed as arenas in which competing approaches to housing policy take shape. The article distinguishes the activities of tenant organisations and the Plataforma de Afectados por la Hipoteca from those of labour unions. Its anthropological argument approaches the home as a setting for kinship, care, memory and belonging. A historical discussion of homeownership in Spain connects the promotion of property ownership under Francoism with contemporary expectations about security and social advancement. The closing reflection considers how family property and inheritance may reproduce inequality, explicitly identifying this discussion as a hypothesis rather than an established finding. The article draws on academic literature, institutional reports and press coverage to explore the conditions required for housing rights to become effective in everyday life. Independent academic essay. This deposit does not constitute a peer-reviewed journal publication.

title: Internal Control as a Mechanism Linking Digital Accounting and Financial Reporting Quality in Nigerian SMEs
summary: ABSTRACT: Digital accounting systems can improve accounting processes, but the organisational value of adoption may depend on how system capabilities interact with internal controls. This study qualitatively explores how SME owners, managers and accountants describe internal control as a mechanism linking digital accounting adoption and financial reporting quality in Lagos State, Nigeria. Thirteen participants were purposively selected from a larger survey of 207 SMEs to provide variation in digital adoption, firm size, sector, internal control effectiveness and financial reporting quality. Semi-structured interviews were conducted and analysed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis. Participants consistently described digital accounting systems as strengthening internal controls through audit trails, segregation of duties, approval workflows, exception reporting and standardised procedures. They also associated stronger controls with improvements in the accuracy, timeliness, reliability and completeness of financial reports. A further theme distinguished more extensive use of dedicated accounting systems from limited use of spreadsheets or unconfigured system features. The findings provide qualitative evidence of a pathway consistent with the proposed mediation model, while recognising that qualitative accounts cannot statistically establish mediation or causal effects. The study contributes by showing how control capabilities are experienced in practice and by developing the concept of shallow adoption as limited use of available accounting-system capabilities. The findings suggest that SME digitalisation programmes should combine software provision with control configuration, staff training and monitoring. Keywords: digital accounting; internal control; financial reporting quality; SMEs; technology adoption.

title: Forecasting Climate and Extreme Weather Disruption Risk at Critical Logistics Nodes: Ports, Corridors, and Inland Gateways
summary: Critical logistics nodes, including major seaports, inland waterway locks, rail gateways, and key highway corridors, concentrate the physical movement of goods that sustain the United States economy and support national security supply chains. Extreme weather events, including hurricanes, flooding, extreme heat, drought related low water, and winter storms, have repeatedly disrupted operations at these nodes, producing cascading delays, inventory shortages, and elevated costs. As the frequency and intensity of certain extremes change, the value of anticipatory disruption forecasting rises. This research project examines how meteorological forecasts, historical disruption records, node specific vulnerability attributes, and network dependency data can be combined into practical early warning and impact estimation tools for logistics planners. The project outlines indicator construction, impact scoring, scenario based stress testing of network consequences, and decision linkages to pre positioning, modal shift, and inventory buffering. The contribution is an applied structure that transportation agencies, port authorities, defense logistics organizations, and private network operators can adapt to improve readiness for weather driven supply stress without requiring perfect event prediction.

title: Financial reporting quality and investment efficiency: the moderating role of audit quality
summary: Purpose This study aims to analyze the influence of financial reporting quality (FRQ) and audit quality (AQ) on firms’ investment efficiency (IE) within an emerging market context and to explore whether AQ acts as a moderating factor in the relationship between FRQ and IE. Design/methodology/approach This study uses panel data from 291 non-financial listed firms in Vietnam covering the years 2014–2023, totaling 2,910 firm-year observations. IE is measured as the residual from an investment model based on growth opportunities. FRQ is created from three measures based on accruals and revenue, along with a composite FRQ index. The models are estimated using feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) and the two-step system generalized method of moments (SGMM). Findings Both FRQ and AQ positively influence IE, with AQ demonstrating greater robustness under SGMM. The interaction between FRQ and AQ is statistically significant and negative, suggesting a partial substitution effect. Research limitations/implications FRQ measurement methods may be subject to estimation errors, and AQ is constrained to a binary Big Four audit firms proxy. Potential self-selection bias and limited generalizability remain considerations. Practical implications Firms not audited by the Big Four audit firms are encouraged to strengthen their FRQ through timely and predictive disclosures. Simultaneously, regulatory authorities should enhance their oversight of audit practices and of IFRS implementation. Social implications Improving FRQ and AQ fosters transparency and efficient capital allocation. Originality/value This study offers new evidence from Vietnam, demonstrating that FRQ and AQ serve as partly substitutive governance mechanisms in emerging markets.

title: Pengaruh Digital Mindset, Trust in Technology, dan Persepsi Risiko terhadap Penggunaan Software Akuntansi pada UMKM di Kota Jayapura
summary: Digital transformation has driven changes in financial management among Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), including the adoption of accounting software. This technology can improve transaction recording accuracy, financial data processing efficiency, and the quality of accounting information. However, the use of accounting software among MSMEs is still influenced by users’ behavioral factors and perceptions. This study aims to analyze the effects of Digital Mindset, Trust in Technology, and perceived risk on accounting software usage among MSMEs in Jayapura City. A quantitative approach with an explanatory research method was employed. Data were collected through questionnaires from 103 MSME owners using convenience and purposive sampling techniques. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS version 4. The results show that Digital Mindset has a positive and significant effect on accounting software usage, with a path coefficient of 0.236 and p = 0.044. Trust in Technology also has a positive and significant effect, with a path coefficient of 0.503 and p = 0.000. In contrast, perceived risk has no significant effect, with a path coefficient of 0.009 and p = 0.938. The R-square value of 0.461 indicates that the three variables jointly explain 46.1% of the variation in accounting software usage. These findings confirm that trust in technology is the most dominant factor encouraging MSMEs in Jayapura City to use accounting software effectively.

title: The Effect of Real Earnings Management, Institutional Ownership, and Other Factors on Firm Value in Indonesia
summary: This study aims to obtain empirical evidence on the effect of institutional ownership, audit committee, real earnings management, profitability, liquidity, firm size, tax avoidance, and independent board of commissioners on firm value. The sample consists of 108 manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2022 to 2024, resulting in 324 observations. Using a quantitative approach with purposive sampling and multiple regression analysis, the results show that profitability and the independent board of commissioners have a positive effect on firm value, while real earnings management and liquidity have a negative effect. Meanwhile, institutional ownership, audit committee, firm size, and tax avoidance have no effect on firm value.

title: Navigating the Digital Divide: An Assessment of AI Adoption Challenges and Strategic Management Frameworks for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria
summary: This systematic review examines the state of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria, identifies principal barriers to adoption, and proposes a pragmatic strategic management framework tailored to Nigeria’s resource environment. We conducted a structured search across Google Scholar, Scopus and Web of Science and screened publications from 2018–2025. 27 peer-reviewed studies and 4 policy/industry reports met inclusion criteria and were synthesised thematically. Findings show that AI adoption in Nigerian SMEs is uneven: digitally enabled firms in fintech and ecommerce are experimenting with chatbots, recommendation systems and automation, while many SMEs lack the basic digital foundations required for scalable AI. The dominant barriers are unreliable digital infrastructure and power, limited data readiness, shortage of AI skills, scarce SME-targeted financing, and regulatory uncertainty. Contradictory evidence indicates that, in contexts where data systems and managerial capacity already exist, modest AI interventions delivered measurable benefits; however, when foundational systems are weak, AI adoption yields minimal gains and can even misallocate scarce resources. The paper concludes with a three-pillar strategic framework—digital capability development, organisational readiness, and ecosystem support alongside practical, staged actions for managers, vendors and policymakers. The review highlights research gaps and recommends pilot evaluations, longitudinal studies and cost–benefit analyses specific to Nigerian SMEs.

title: Gestión del talento humano por competencias aplicada para la adaptación a la transformación digital en el Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Municipal del cantón Pasaje
summary: Digital transformation represents a challenge for public institutions, as it requires strengthening human talent competencies to respond to technological and organizational changes. The objective of this research was to determine the relationship between competency-based human talent management and adaptation to digital transformation in the Municipal Autonomous Decentralized Government of Pasaje Canton. A quantitative, applied study with a descriptive-correlational scope and a non-experimental cross-sectional design was conducted. The sample consisted of 35 public servants selected through non-probabilistic purposive sampling. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. The results showed a favorable perception of competency-based human talent management (mean = 3.81/5) and adaptation to digital transformation (mean = 3.82/5). The correlation between both variables was positive and weak (p = 0.261), but not statistically significant (p = 0.130 > 0.05). Consequently, no sufficient statistical evidence was found to establish an association between competency-based human talent management and adaptation to digital transformation in the study sample. The descriptive results suggest that, in addition to human talent management practices, digital adaptation may be related to organizational, technological, and cultural factors that were not included in the analysis. Keywords: human talent management; competency-based management; digital transformation; public sector; digital competencies.

title: Understanding bidi industry from the lenses of bidi workforce: an exploratory study
summary: INTRODUCTION: Bidis (small hand-rolled cigarillos) account for 85% of smoked tobacco products in India. The bidi industry is criticised for health hazards, economic exploitation, poor social security, long hours, low wages and contractualisation. This study examines bidi industry practices in India and how these allow it to resist tobacco control measures. METHODS: (middle-men/intermediaries), community/youth club representatives and labour union leaders, with assistance from 10 'champions' (trusted community insiders). Participants provided informed consent and their confidentiality was ensured. Interview data, in Bangla and Hindi, were translated into English and then analysed thematically. FINDINGS: Five major themes emerged. First, bidi companies engage in image-building corporate social responsibility activities that mirror tactics used by multinational cigarette companies, creating a facade of social responsibility while exploiting workers. Second, the industry systematically violates government policies through wage discrepancies, provident fund fraud and false worker registration to evade compliance. Third, systemic inequity pervades the sector, with median wages at only 38-53% of government-mandated rates. Fourth, unjustified bidi rejections facilitate widespread illicit trade that evades taxation and government oversight. Fifth, child labour remains entrenched in West Bengal. CONCLUSION: Bidi companies' current practices perpetuate labour exploitation and illicit trade. We recommend uniform national guidelines that require transparent operations and mandatory registration of all bidi rollers.

title: VERS UN MODÈLE DE MATURITÉ DE LA RESPONSABILITÉ NUMÉRIQUE DES ORGANISATIONS PUBLIQUES : L'AUDIT SOCIAL COMME DISPOSITIF DE PILOTAGE
summary: RÉSUMÉ La responsabilité numérique des organisations (RNO) s'est imposée, depuis le début des années 2020, comme un prolongement de la responsabilité sociétale des organisations appliqué à la sphère numérique. Si la littérature récente en documente les principes, elle demeure largement silencieuse sur la question du pilotage : comment une organisation publique passe-t-elle d'initiatives numériques dispersées et non formalisées à une démarche structurée, gouvernée et évaluable ? Cet article conceptuel propose de répondre à cette lacune en construisant un modèle de maturité de la RNO à quatre niveaux informel, sensibilisé, structuré et piloté spécifiquement adapté aux établissements et entreprises publics (EEP) marocains. Il positionne l'audit social non comme un simple outil de contrôle a posteriori, mais comme le dispositif de transition qui permet à l'organisation de progresser d'un niveau de maturité au suivant. Prolongeant un travail empirique antérieur qui avait mis en évidence le caractère spontané et peu coordonné des pratiques numériques responsables dans les EEP marocains, l'article articule une revue de la littérature, une modélisation théorique et un ensemble de propositions de recherche destinées à être testées empiriquement. La contribution est double : sur le plan théorique, elle enrichit le champ émergent de la RNO d'une grille de lecture développementale ; sur le plan managérial, elle offre aux dirigeants publics un référentiel d'auto-positionnement et de progression. Mots clés : responsabilité numérique des organisations ; audit social ; modèle de maturité ; secteur public ; établissements et entreprises publics ; gouvernance numérique. ABSTRACT Organizational Digital Responsibility (ODR) has emerged, since the early 2020s, as an extension of corporate social responsibility applied to the digital sphere. While recent scholarship documents its principles, it remains largely silent on the question of steering: how does a public organization move from scattered, informal digital initiatives towards a structured, governed and measurable approach? This conceptual paper addresses this gap by building a four-level ODR maturity model informal, aware, structured and steered specifically tailored to Moroccan public establishments and enterprises (PEE). It positions social auditing not as a mere ex-post control tool, but as the transition mechanism that enables an organization to progress from one maturity level to the next. Extending prior empirical work that highlighted the spontaneous and poorly coordinated nature of responsible digital practices in Moroccan PEEs, the paper combines a literature review, a theoretical model and a set of research propositions intended for future empirical testing. The contribution is twofold: theoretically, it enriches the emerging ODR field with a developmental lens; managerially, it offers public managers a self-assessment and progression framework. Keywords: organizational digital responsibility; social auditing; maturity model; public sector; public establishments and enterprises; digital governance.

title: Green finance influences financial stability through nonlinear dynamics in BRICS countries with FinTech and financial development as complementary drivers
summary: Green finance is expanding rapidly across the BRICS economies, yet little is known about whether this expansion supports or strains their banking systems. This paper examines the relationship between green finance and banking stability, as measured by the Z-score, in Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa over 2005–2024. The question is whether that relationship is nonlinear and whether FinTech adoption and financial depth change the point at which it bends. What the paper adds to studies that treat these variables one at a time is a direct estimate of the curvature and a threshold expressed as a function of the two moderators rather than as a single number. A two-step system GMM estimator is applied to linear and quadratic specifications, the latter adding the square of green finance, as well as its interactions with FinTech development and financial depth. The quadratic model indicates an inverted U-shaped relationship: the linear term is positive (0.042), and the squared term is negative (− 12.603 × 10 −6 ), which places the unconditional turning point at about 1666 units of the green finance indicator, slightly above the sample mean. Both interaction terms are positive and significant, so the turning point moves to the right as FinTech adoption and financial depth increase (from roughly 2400 to 3870 units across the scenarios examined). Dumitrescu–Hurlin tests indicate two-way causality between stability and each of its determinants. Because the panel contains only five countries, the GMM results are read as indicative rather than definitive, and they are cross-checked against second-generation unit root, cointegration and structural-break tests that date the main shifts to 2008–2011 and 2021. Given the size of the panel and the unverified comparability of the green finance and FinTech series across countries, the policy message is conditional: green finance appears compatible with banking stability at the levels observed in most BRICS countries, but its marginal benefit shrinks at high levels. The room for safe expansion depends on the digital and financial infrastructure that accompanies it.

title: Governing circular intellectual capital disclosure: evidence from European banks
summary: Purpose The aim of this study is twofold. First, it seeks to examine the level of circular intellectual capital (CIC) information disseminated by European banks through their official websites. Second, it aims to investigate the role of corporate governance in shaping CIC disclosure (CICD). Specifically, this study examines the impact of board size, board gender diversity, board independence, and the presence of a sustainability committee on the level of CICD through the lens of stakeholder–agency theory. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a manual content analysis of the official websites of 120 European listed banks in order to measure the level of CICD. Econometric analyses are then conducted to investigate the impact of corporate governance on CICD practices. Findings The findings show that European banks still disclose a limited amount of CIC-related information through their official websites. Additionally, this study demonstrates that board size, board gender diversity, and board independence positively affect the level of CICD, whereas the presence of a sustainability committee has no significant effect on this type of disclosure. Practical implications The findings suggest that banks should strengthen the communication of CIC-related information through their official websites and pay greater attention to board composition, as larger, more gender-diverse, and more independent boards appear to foster higher levels of CICD. This study also provides useful insights for policymakers, regulators, and standard setters by highlighting the need for more structured guidance to support the disclosure of CIC-related information in the banking sector. For higher education institutions, the findings highlight the importance of integrating CIC and CICD into higher education curricula. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature on non-financial disclosure in the banking sector by introducing CICD as a novel and analytically distinct construct within this context. It also extends research on the relationship between corporate governance and non-financial disclosure to this emerging form of disclosure and broadens the application of stakeholder–agency theory to the domain of CICD.

title: The Effect of Employee Attitudes Toward NGOs and Helping Others on Satisfaction and Loyalty: The Mediating Role of Employee Volunteering
summary: Companies increasingly recognize the reputational implications of corporate social responsibility and adopt various practices to strengthen employee loyalty and satisfaction. Employee volunteering is a widely adopted practice in this process, yet it remains a relatively underexplored research area. This study investigates the relationship between employee attitudes, specifically toward NGOs and helping others, and employee satisfaction and loyalty, while examining the mediating role of employee volunteering. A large-scale quantitative study was conducted via computer-assisted personal communication with 301 employees who participated in volunteering programs at charitable companies. The proposed model was tested using structural equation modeling. Results indicate that attitudes toward helping others positively predict employee volunteering, which is in turn positively associated with employee satisfaction and loyalty, and employee volunteering mediates this relationship. However, attitudes toward NGOs do not significantly predict employee volunteering, and the corresponding mediation was not supported. The study offers theoretical and practical insights for researchers and practitioners.

title: AI Adoption and Remote Teaching Supply Chain Efficiency
summary: With the ongoing digital transformation of education and the pervasive integration of artificial intelligence, the remote teaching supply chain has emerged as a critical backbone supporting the flow of online educational resources, the delivery of instructional services, and the implementation of talent cultivation. Optimizing the efficiency of this supply chain is essential for addressing key practical challenges, including resource misallocation, procedural redundancies, and insufficient coordination in online education. Grounded in technology acceptance theory, this study investigates how basic artificial intelligence adoption and advanced artificial intelligence adoption influence remote teaching supply chain efficiency, as well as the moderating effect of the digital technology environment. Based on an analysis of 206 valid survey responses from practitioners in universities, vocational colleges, and online education institutions, both basic and advanced artificial intelligence adoption exert positive effects on remote teaching supply chain efficiency. In addition, the digital technology environment positively moderates the relationships between basic artificial intelligence adoption and supply chain efficiency, as well as between advanced artificial intelligence adoption and supply chain efficiency. Finally, theoretical guidance and managerial implications are provided for the intelligent development of educational institutions and platforms, as well as for the optimization of remote teaching supply chains.

title: Analisis Kesesuaian Pembiayaan Musyarakah dengan Prinsip Keuangan dalam Islam di PT BPR Syariah Meru Nusantara Mandiri (BNU Syariah)
summary: Musyarakah financing is one of the partnership-based financing schemes in Islamic banking that emphasizes the principles of justice, transparency, profit and loss sharing, and risk sharing. However, its implementation often faces challenges related to business monitoring, financial reporting, and customers' understanding of Islamic financing principles. This study aims to analyze the implementation of the musyarakah contract at PT BPR Syariah Meru Nusantara Mandiri from the perspective of Islamic finance principles. This research employed a qualitative approach with a field research design. Primary data were collected through observations, semi-structured interviews with bank officers, and documentation, while secondary data were obtained from regulations, DSN-MUI Fatwas, books, and relevant scientific literature. The collected data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, consisting of data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings reveal that the implementation of the musyarakah contract has generally complied with Islamic principles and the DSN-MUI Fatwa No. 08/DSN-MUI/IV/2000 concerning Musyarakah Financing. The principles of justice, transparency, sharia compliance, profit and loss sharing, and risk sharing have been implemented in financing activities. Nevertheless, several challenges remain, including limited financial literacy among customers, inadequate business financial records, and constraints in monitoring financing activities. Therefore, strengthening customer education, improving monitoring systems, and optimizing financial reporting are essential to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of musyarakah financing.

title: A Study on North-South Rule Conflicts in the Global Climate Governance System
summary: Frequent extreme climate events across the globe underscore the urgency of the global climate governance system. Within the current global climate governance system centered on the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), several principles and mechanisms coexist: differentiated responsibilities, Kyoto flexibility mechanisms, and the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. Nevertheless, divergences persist between developed and developing countries regarding the delineation of historical responsibilities, guarantee of financial inputs, transfer of green technologies, and the right to development. Some unilateral climate measures have prompted debate about their compatibility with multilateral frameworks, which may widen the North-South trust gap and fragments the global climate governance system. After analyzing the dilemmas embedded in the existing governance regime, this paper proposes three pathways for reforming the global climate governance system: accelerating the establishment of a more equitable accounting system, strengthening the coordination and binding force of existing rules, and promptly addressing the shortfalls in finance and technology transfer.

title: Comercio electrónico e infraestructura tecnológica: análisis comparativo entre México y Centroamérica
summary: Globalization has driven the rise of the digital economy and electronic commerce, creating new dynamics of international competitiveness. This article provides a comparative analysis of the technological infrastructure conditions in Mexico, Costa Rica, Guatemala, and El Salvador between 2019 and 2025, focusing on connectivity, cybersecurity, digital payment systems, and technology infrastructure (data centers). The methodology is documentary, based on official sources from international organizations and national authorities. Findings reveal differentiated progress in digitalization and online services, but also significant gaps in infrastructure, regulation, and technical capacities. The study concludes that these disparities affect the ability of countries to integrate into international digital markets, and that regional cooperation in connectivity, cybersecurity, and cross-border payments represents a strategic contribution to International Relations by strengthening digital integration andglobal governance of electronic commerce.

title: Topology-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Credit Card Fraud Detection: Integrating Multidimensional Rebalancing with Deep Q-Networks
summary: Background Credit card fraud detection faces extreme class imbalance, concept drift, and topological overlap. Standard Deep Q-Networks (DQN) suffer catastrophic performance degradation (e.g., 26.8% precision) due to noisy reward signals from overlapping decision boundaries. Methods We propose the Adaptive Multidimensional Rebalancing Deep Q- Network (AMR-DQN). It integrates topology-aware data filtering directly into the DQN Experience Replay Buffer, dynamically evaluating local density, class overlap, and feature variability to weight state transitions. A cost-sensitive reward function explicitly aligns the reinforcement learning objective with institutional profitability. Results On the Kaggle Credit Card Fraud dataset, AMR-DQN achieved an F2- Score of 0.859 and AUPRC of 0.883, outperforming the strongest baseline (SMOTE- ENN + XGBoost) by 5.9% and 12.1%. It converged 43% faster than standard DQN and generated the highest Expected Fraud Loss Reduction (EFLR) of $46,750.50 per 10,000 transactions. Ablation studies revealed that removing topological constraints harms business profitability despite marginal statistical gains. Conclusions AMR-DQN bridges the gap between sequential machine learning and profit-centric financial objectives. By leveraging SHAP-based Explainable AI, it ensures regulatory compliance while providing a robust, scalable solution for adap- tive fraud detection in dynamic FinTech environments.

title: How International Trade and Global Value Chains Reshape Environmental Sustainability
summary: The expansion of international trade and global value chains has transformed the geographical organization of production while redistributing environmental pressures across countries, sectors and stages of production. This paper examines the relationship between trade integration, global value-chain participation and environmental sustainability through three complementary dimensions. First, it considers how trade liberalization affects pollution, embodied carbon, natural-resource use, water pressures and biodiversity through scale, composition and technique effects. Second, it examines the environmental consequences of global value-chain participation, focusing on value-chain position, technological upgrading, supplier capabilities, lead-firm governance and multi-tier sustainability management. Third, it considers the institutional mechanisms through which trade policy can contribute to environmental governance, including environmental provisions in trade agreements, carbon border adjustment mechanisms and trade in environmental goods. The literature indicates that international integration does not produce a uniform environmental outcome. Trade can expand production and shift ecological pressures across borders, but it can also promote cleaner technologies, productivity improvements and environmental upgrading when appropriate regulatory, technological and organizational conditions are present. Sustainable globalization therefore depends on the interaction between trade policies, domestic environmental regulation, value-chain governance, technological capacity and international cooperation. Environmental policy must consequently address both territorial emissions and the ecological pressures embodied in internationally fragmented production and consumption networks.

title: Psychological strengths and career adaptability among Indonesian professional accountants in the era of Society 5.0
summary: The accounting profession is facing very rapid changes due to technological disruption. This change is being examined from a psychological perspective, questioning whether these changes indeed bring more positive impacts in the form of opportunities to grow, develop, learn, and flourish, rather than threats. Grounded in the framework of psychology, this study investigates whether psychological strengths such as a proactive personality, self-esteem, goal orientation, and occupational prestige can enhance career adaptability among Indonesian accountants. The study aims to understand how these strengths enable professionals to thrive amid digital transformation in the era of Society 5.0. Using a quantitative survey approach with 149 professional accountants, the data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) PLS. The results show that proactive personality and goal orientation significantly predict career adaptability, both directly and indirectly through self-esteem. These findings extend the understanding of psychological theory by demonstrating that psychological strengths foster resilience, adaptability, and flourishing in professional contexts. Implications for organizations and accounting education are discussed to promote strength-based interventions and lifelong adaptability in digitalized work environments.

title: GREEN FINANCE AND CAPITAL CIRCULATION IN SMART AGRICULTURE: AI-DRIVEN INSIGHTS
summary: This scientific article examines the role of digitalization and smart agriculture in advancing green finance, AI-driven innovation, and inclusive rural investment. The main objective of the study is to assess how integrating digital technologies and AI systems into agricultural finance can enhance productivity and support sustainable community development. Drawing on the theoretical foundations of digital finance, green finance, and development policy, the research explores the relationship between traditional credit systems and innovative technological solutions to drive structural transformations in rural economies. The analysis shows that conventional agricultural finance mechanisms are often constrained by limited access to funds, high transaction costs, and insufficient risk management. Digital tools, including mobile banking, fintech platforms, and AI-based credit scoring, improve financial accessibility, optimize investment decisions, and increase transparency, while smart agricultural technologies enhance efficiency, productivity, and climate resilience. The study also discusses long-term trends in global agro-food trade and regional structural characteristics reflecting uneven import and export flows across regions. Overall, the research demonstrates that combining digitalization, AI, and targeted finance can significantly foster more sustainable and productive agricultural development, increasing both efficiency and financial inclusion while supporting long-term resilience in rural communities.

title: Інституційний, регуляторний та поведінковий виміри управління капіталом банку: бібліометричний і тематичний аналіз
summary: Bank capital management supports financial resilience, loss absorption and adaptation to shocks. Yet research is fragmented across prudential regulation, institutional mechanisms and behavioural aspects of decision-making. This article systematises the conceptual and thematic structure of bank capital management research and assesses how regulatory, institutional and behavioural dimensions are represented and connected. Bibliometric and thematic mapping uses 1,521 Scopus-indexed documents. In VOSviewer, the primary network is based on author-keyword co-occurrence with lexical normalisation; a supplementary term network is derived from titles and abstracts in the same corpus. A coding dictionary classifies markers across the three dimensions. Structural asymmetry is assessed by marker occurrences, total link strength, cluster distribution and cluster-core formation. The primary network comprises 147 keywords in 12 clusters; the supplementary analysis identifies four broader macro-domains. Regulatory issues occupy the central position: their markers have the highest occurrence and link-strength values and form the core of two clusters. They connect closely with financial resilience, liquidity, lending and risk. The institutional dimension is crosscutting, represented by corporate governance, ownership structure, supervision, market discipline and deposit insurance. Behavioural markers, including risk-taking, moral hazard, regulatory arbitrage and executive compensation, form no autonomous core but are embedded in regulatory, risk-related and corporate-governance themes. The study’s novelty lies in jointly operationalising and analysing the three dimensions within one bibliometric design, identifying a consolidated regulatory core, a cross-cutting institutional dimension, a dispersed behavioural dimension and their interrelationships. The findings offer thematic reference points for research, regulatory analysis and bank capital planning. Limitations include reliance on one database and metadata, inclusion of dimension markers in the search query, and sensitivity to selection and clustering parameters. Article type: empirical.

title: Cognitive Diversity and Performance of Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
summary: Cognitive diversity has become an important corporate governance issue because boards and management teams increasingly operate in complex and uncertain business environments that require varied knowledge, experience, skills, perspectives, and problem-solving approaches. This study examines the relationship between cognitive diversity and performance of deposit money banks in Nigeria. The study adopts a conceptual and review-based approach, drawing on contemporary empirical studies on board diversity, expertise, educational background, professional experience and financial performance in Nigeria and other emerging markets. The literature indicates that cognitive diversity can improve decision quality, monitoring effectiveness, innovation, risk assessment and strategic responsiveness by reducing groupthink and broadening the range of alternatives considered by decision makers. However, excessive diversity without effective communication, inclusion and leadership may increase conflict and slow decision processes. Recent Nigerian studies provide mixed but increasingly supportive evidence that board expertise, age, gender and other diversity dimensions can influence financial performance. The paper therefore argues that the performance benefits of cognitive diversity depend not simply on having heterogeneous directors but on effectively integrating their knowledge and expertise into strategic decision-making. The study recommends competence based board appointments, continuous professional development, inclusive leadership and stronger governance mechanisms for deposit money banks operating in Nigeria.

title: Strengthening Tarif Principles Embeddedness in Pertamina's STK: A Governance Assessment of Framework
summary: Background: Corporate governance is effective only when policy-level principles are translated into observable operational requirements. In large state-owned enterprises, strong formal governance can coexist with incomplete procedural embeddedness, creating a governance translation gap. Objective: This study evaluates the embeddedness of Transparency, Accountability, Responsibility, Independency, and Fairness (TARIF) principles in PT Pertamina (Persero)’s Sistem Tata Kerja (STK), using procurement planning as a pilot case. Methods: An action-research-oriented qualitative case design combined systematic document analysis, corporate risk and governance records, and practitioner validation. Nine procedural elements were mapped against five TARIF principles, producing 45 element–principle combinations rated as present, partial, enhancement opportunity, or not applicable. Results: Overall governance coverage was 56%. Responsibility was the strongest principle, at 89%, whereas Independency was the weakest, at 11%, revealing gaps in conflict-of-interest controls, separation of duties, and independent review. The most consequential gaps occurred in needs identification and supporting documentation for vendor selection. Alternative C+ received the strongest overall evaluation. Conclusion: The findings show that governance quality should be assessed not only through policy-level compliance but also through explicit procedural mechanisms. The TARIF-to-STK Governance Enhancement Framework operationalizes the policy-to-procedure distance and provides a structured basis for targeted improvement. Theoretically, it extends governance assessment toward procedure-level embeddedness; practically, it supports repeatable STK review and prioritization. Because the evidence derives from a single procurement-planning case, broader applicability requires validation across other STKs and longitudinal assessment of implementation effects.

title: Reimagining work in ageing societies: AI-enabled reskilling and the power of future work identities
summary: With an ageing population and fast development of AI, the labour force is drastically changing, which presents a need to understand how older adults experience and respond to technologically evolving work environments. Based on Possible Selves Theory, this research investigates how older adults understand the function of AI-enabled digital reskilling to inform future workforce possible selves and continued participation in employment in later life. Data were collected from 51 older adults via the Prolific Academic platform and were analysed using the Gioia methodology. Findings revealed that older adults view AI-enabled digital reskilling as a significant pathway to help them create their future workforce possible selves, which acts as an important motivation for continued participation in the workforce. Additionally, older adults evaluate their future working identities in terms of their expected ability, the likelihood of success, their skill sets, confidence, labour market opportunities, and age-related constraints. Thus, this study extends Possible Selves Theory by demonstrating how AI-enabled digital reskilling shapes future work identities and supports workforce adaptation in later life. The findings further suggest that organizations, policymakers, and digital platform designers should invest in accessible AI-enabled digital reskilling initiatives that foster workforce participation and promote inclusive ageing in the digital economy.

title: Capital Structure Decisions and Financial Performance of Firms Listed in the Alternative Investment Market Segment of the Nairobi Securities Exchange.
summary: Financial performance, reflected in profitability, liquidity and market valuation, is a critical measure of the sustainability and growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) listed on the Alternative Investment Market Segment (AIMS) of the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Despite relaxed listing requirements and tax incentives intended to widen SME access to public capital, AIMS-listed firms continue to face thin market liquidity, high perceived investment risk, limited access to affordable long-term debt and governance gaps, with the segment accounting for less than 5% of total NSE market capitalization and more than 60% of its firms reporting volatile or declining profits between 2019 and 2024. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between capital structure decisions and financial performance among firms listed on AIMS. It specifically examined the influence of debt-based financing, equity-based financing, hybrid financing and retained earnings-based financing on financial performance. The study was anchored on the Static Trade-Off Theory, Agency Cost Theory, Market Timing Theory and Pecking Order Theory. A descriptive and explanatory cross-sectional research design was adopted, targeting all nine AIMS-listed firms through a census, from which five finance and strategic decision-makers per firm were purposively selected, giving a sample of 45 respondents. Primary data were collected using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire and were supplemented with secondary data from audited financial statements. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods, namely Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis, were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four financing decisions jointly explained 44.8% of the variation in financial performance (F = 3.236, p = 0.027). Hybrid financing had the strongest positive and significant influence on financial performance, followed by debt-based financing, while equity-based financing and retained earnings-based financing had positive and significant but comparatively smaller influences. The study, therefore, recommends that AIMS-listed firms should adopt balanced and well-monitored debt strategies aligned with cash flow capacity, expand equity financing while carefully managing dilution, prioritize hybrid instruments such as convertible securities to enhance flexibility and cost efficiency, and strengthen profit retention and reinvestment policies complemented by external financing.

title: Digital transformation and universities
summary: The general objective of the research was to determine the advances related to digital transformation and universities. The specific objective of the research was to identify the best global universities that use digital transformation. Methodology, in this research, 33 documents have been selected, carried out in the period 2018 - 2026; including: scientific articles, review articles and information from websites of recognized organizations. Results, digital transformation has a positive impact on universities worldwide and is becoming an outstanding challenge in our Latin American countries. Digital transformation offers great opportunities and challenges to organizations, especially those in higher education, providing them with tools to fulfill their mission. Universities play an important role in society. With the rise of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, their impact and the new challenges they face must be evaluated. Conclusions, about the general objective of the research, universities are undergoing a process of digital transformation; therefore, they need to invest in infrastructure, technology, innovation, and staff training in order to become digital universities. title: A socio-technical mechanism of the agricultural digital divide: Ecuador within a heterogeneous Latin American context
summary: Digital agriculture can improve farm management, resource-use efficiency, and decision-making; however, access to technology alone does not guarantee equivalent economic benefits. This perspective article conceptualizes the agricultural digital divide as a socio-technical and economic inequality that can arise along a sequence linking structural conditions, resource accessibility, capability formation, technological appropriation, productive integration, economic value realization, and value capture and benefit distribution. This definition extends the analysis beyond connectivity and adoption by considering whether agricultural actors can integrate technologies into viable productive activities and retain a significant share of the value generated. Institutions, extension services, cooperatives, financing mechanisms, technology providers, business models, and data governance can shape the transitions between these stages. Ecuador is examined as a focal analytical case within a heterogeneous Latin America, without assuming regional representativeness. The framework redirects the evaluation of digitalization away from the number of technologies deployed and toward their productive appropriation, economic viability, and the distribution of their benefits, thereby reinforcing the relationship between digital transformation and agricultural economics.

title: Circular logistics as part of the supply chain
summary: This paper investigates circular logistics and its impact on the efficiency and sustainability of the supply chain. Key trends from 2019 to 2024 are analyzed, including the adoption of advanced technologies such as Blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), and artificial intelligence (AI), as well as recycling and material reuse, simplified product returns, and sustainable packaging. A qualitative analysis of secondary data, including scholarly articles and company reports, shows that the implementation of circular logistics reduces operational costs and waste, while its success depends on developed recycling infrastructure and the adaptation of business models. The study connects circular economy theory with practical examples, provides insights into the challenges and success factors in integrating circular models into supply chains, and offers guidance for future research and practical application.

title: Reinforcement learning for adaptive supplier sustainability scoring and sourcing share adjustment in ready made garment supply chains
summary: Global supply chains face increasing legal, commercial, and stakeholder pressure to verify supplier sustainability rather than rely only on supplier claims. This study develops a safety-gated tabular Q-learning framework for adaptive supplier scoring, limited sourcing-share adjustment, and audit targeting in a stylized Bangladesh ready-made garment sourcing portfolio. The simulation distinguishes direct exporters, subcontractors, and small or informal suppliers; represents safety, labour, and environmental performance separately; prohibits rewards when verified safety or labour falls below 0.60; and imposes a minimum annual audit. Three independently trained agents were evaluated in 75 paired out-of-sample replications against a contextual bandit, a risk-based adaptive heuristic, a static threshold, a combined scheduled-audit-and-threshold policy, scheduled auditing, and random action. Q-learning achieved mean true compliance of 0.862 compared with 0.820 under the static threshold, increased the share of suppliers at or above 0.80 from 58.2 to 81.3%, and reduced mean severe incidents from 3.29 to 1.71. It used 167 audits compared with 362 for the combined scheduled-audit-and-threshold policy, a 53.8% reduction, while mean procurement cost was 1.1% higher than under the static threshold. The contextual bandit produced lower compliance (0.742) and more incidents (2.96), supporting the value of delayed-action learning. The risk-based heuristic produced statistically similar mean compliance but required 55 additional audits and yielded a narrower compliant-supplier share. Paired tests, effect sizes, convergence diagnostics, supplier-stratum results, credit-assignment ablation, time-state testing, and multi-parameter robustness analyses are reported. The findings remain simulation evidence rather than factory-level validation, but they provide a reproducible and technically strengthened test of adaptive supplier governance.

title: DIGITAL GOVERNANCE IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES: EVOLUTION, NOT REVOLUTION — AN INCLUSIVE AND SUSTAINABLE PATHWAY
summary: This research paper explores how digital governance is reshaping public services, information management, and citizen engagement in developing nations. While the shift to digital tools offers significant opportunities to improve transparency and monitoring, it also presents critical challenges—including deep-rooted digital divides, weak institutional readiness, administrative resistance, and rising cybersecurity risks. Through a qualitative analysis of academic literature and policy frameworks, this study argues that a successful digital transformation cannot be treated as a purely technological upgrade. Instead, its success depends heavily on the capacity of both public institutions and citizens to adapt. The paper advocates for a practical "Evolution, Not Revolution" approach. Rather than rushing into large-scale, rushed digitalization without adequate preparation, governments should gradually strengthen infrastructure, secure data privacy, implement inclusive access safeguards, and evaluate outcomes in stages. Ultimately, a paced and well-prepared transition ensures that digital governance creates lasting public value that is truly inclusive, secure, and sustainable.
