title: Factors Affecting the Informal Sector and its Relationship with Sustainable Development in Egypt
summary: (1) Background: This research aims to study the factors influencing the informal sector in Egypt and analyze their relationships with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) within the framework of Egypt’s Vision 2030. (2) Methods: The research is based on an integrated scientific methodology combining quantitative and qualitative analysis, utilizing secondary data from official statistics and international organization reports, in addition to primary field data collected through questionnaires and interviews. (3) Results: The study highlights the role of economic factors, such as limited income and non-inclusive economic growth, in driving labor towards informal employment. It also illustrates the impact of social and demographic factors, including gender, age, and educational level, in determining individuals’ opportunities to engage in the informal sector. The research further reveals that the poor quality of education and vocational training contributes to the reproduction of informal labor and limits its opportunities for transitioning to formal work. The levels of informal employment are also affected by institutional and regulatory factors, such as administrative complexity, weak governance, the multiplicity of regulatory bodies, and limited trust in formal institutions. The research also shows that digital technological transformation presents an opportunity to expand informal work patterns, but it raises challenges for labor protection and integration into the legal framework. Environmental and spatial factors play a role in promoting the fragility of livelihoods and pushing individuals toward informal work, especially in rural areas, unplanned settlements, and in the context of climate change. The research reveals a close interrelation between these factors and the achievement of the SDGs, such as No Poverty, Decent Work and Economic Growth, Reduced Inequalities, Quality Education, strong institutions, digital transformation, and environmental sustainability. The findings emphasize that addressing the informal sector requires comprehensive, integrated policies that consider all economic, social, educational, institutional, technological, and environmental factors to ensure the achievement of inclusive and sustainable development. (4) Conclusions: The discussion concludes that addressing the informal sector requires comprehensive and integrated policies that account for all influencing factors. Focus must be placed on formalizing the sector, improving the quality of education and training, enhancing governance, utilizing technology, and considering environmental factors. Such an approach effectively and sustainably supports the realization of the SDGs and Egypt Vision (2030).

title: AI-induced corporate social responsibility (AICSR) and e-retailing: a game-changing strategy or a gimmick to attain customer loyalty
summary: Purpose This study examines the direct and mediated effects of AI-induced corporate social responsibility (AICSR) initiatives on customer loyalty in e-retailing, grounded in an integrated theoretical framework of stakeholder theory and signaling theory. It clarifies whether AICSR fosters customer loyalty directly or indirectly via a series of intervening pathways. Design/methodology/approach We tested the framework using cross-sectional survey data collected from 234 active Chinese online retail consumers, and analyzed the dataset via partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS 4. Findings Results reveal that AICSR exerts a significant positive direct effect on customer loyalty. Meanwhile, its influence is transmitted through six constructs – retailer service quality, customer satisfaction, electronic word-of-mouth (e-WOM), retailer image, retailer reputation and customer trust – through both individual mediation pathways and a sequential pathway involving all six mediators. These mediators exhibit significant positive relationships, highlighting their interconnected roles in explaining customer loyalty. Originality/value This study extends extant literature by unpacking the paradox of legitimate distinctiveness amid AICSR in the e-commerce industry. It demonstrates that the effectiveness of AICSR initiatives extends beyond their direct contribution to customer loyalty, revealing the interconnected mechanisms through which AI-induced CSR can generate broader customer value.

title: STRATEGIC HUMAN CAPITAL MANAGEMENT AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE: THE ROLE OF HR ANALYTICS, EMPLOYEE DEVELOPMENT AND STRATEGIC ALIGNMENT
summary: This article examines the mechanisms through which strategic human capital management can improve organizational performance in the context of digital transformation. The study conceptualizes human capital not simply as an organizational resource but as a strategic capability whose value depends on the alignment of employee competencies, development practices, analytical capabilities, and organizational strategy. Based on a critical analysis of recent academic literature, the article proposes an integrated framework linking strategic human capital management with organizational performance through three complementary mechanisms: strategic alignment, employee development, and HR analytics. The analysis demonstrates that employee development strengthens the organization’s ability to convert individual knowledge and competencies into collective performance, while HR analytics enables evidence-based decisions concerning recruitment, development, retention, and workforce allocation. Strategic alignment provides the organizational mechanism through which these practices are connected with long-term objectives. The proposed framework contributes to strategic human resource management research by integrating human capital development and data-driven HR decision-making within a single performance-oriented model. The findings provide a theoretical basis for further empirical research and practical recommendations for organizations seeking to strengthen human capital as a source of sustainable competitive advantage.

title: Geopolitical risk and accounting conservatism: does financial reporting opacity matter? Evidence from an emerging market
summary: As global markets increasingly navigate extreme external shocks, understanding how macroeconomic turbulence reshapes corporate financial reporting strategies remains a critical challenge for stakeholders. This study investigates the empirical relationship between macro-level geopolitical risk (GPR) and accounting conservatism (AC), while examining the moderating role of financial reporting opacity (FRO) in an emerging market setting. Using a panel data sample of 100 non-financial Egyptian Exchange companies spanning 2018–2024 (700 firm-year observations), the analysis employs a random-effects panel regression with year- and firm-clustered standard errors to accommodate the macro-level nature of the GPR index. The findings provide robust empirical evidence that GPR is positively associated with AC. Furthermore, FRO acts as a key moderating factor, significantly strengthening this positive association. This demonstrates that under heightened macro-geopolitical exposure, accounting conservatism strongly aligns with strategic shock absorption and compensatory signaling. The demand for conservative reporting increases more steeply in response to GPR when firm-level financial information is ambiguous, bridging critical information gaps. These empirical associations remain consistent across sensitivity and endogeneity specifications. Overall, the findings offer vital implications for regulators enhancing transparency mandates during crises, and for investors utilizing conservatism as an indicator of managerial prudence in volatile economies.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chain Management.
summary: This paper investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in supply chain management, highlighting the main challenges and opportunities of its application and developing recommendations for practice. It adopts a qualitative method, an interpretivist philosophy and a deductive approach. Primary data were collected through open-ended interviews with nineteen supply chain managers and analysed using narrative analysis. Secondary data were drawn from peer-reviewed journal articles published since 2012 and analysed thematically. The findings indicate that AI is steadily taking a larger role in the supply chain, improving the accuracy of demand forecasting and order fulfilment. AI-enabled robots and machines also reduce human error and improve workplace safety. However, the energy and cost involved can raise operational investment, and many developers are deterred by the power demands of deep learning. Introducing systems to the workforce early, with equal training for everyone, can significantly speed up adoption. This paper is condensed from an MSc applied dissertation completed at the University of Salford (2021/2022), supervised by Dr Langes Supramaniam.

title: Digitalization and Production Processes Re-Engineering in Rivers State Agro Based Industries
summary: The study determined the relationship between digitalization and production processes reengineering in Rivers State agro‑based industries. The objective of the study was to ascertain the relationship between the dimensions of digitalization, such as operations automation and digital connectivity, and production processes re-engineering in Rivers State agro‑based industries, especially in terms of process efficiency improvement and product quality enhancement. The study was anchored on Socio-Technical Theory. The population of the study consisted of sixteen (16) agro-allied firms operating in Rivers State. The entire population of sixteen (16) agro-allied firms operating in Rivers State, was made the sample size of the study. This made the study a census research. As pertaining to respondents, top managers were selected from each of the firms, which gave a total of 79 respondents. Cronbach Alpha was used to ascertain the reliability of the instrument. A total of 79 copies of the questionnaire was administered and 79 copies were retrieved. The primary data obtained from the field were analyzed using Pearson Product Moment Correlation in SPSS version 27.0 for the bivariate analysis. The result of the analyses showed that there is a very strong positive relationship between the dimensions of digitalization, such as operations automation and digital connectivity, and measures of production processes reengineering in Rivers State agro‑based industries, such as process efficiency improvement and product quality enhancement. The study concluded that digital transformation is not merely a technological upgrade but a strategic imperative for sustainable productivity and competitiveness. Therefore, the study recommended amongst others, that agro-based industries should fully integrate automated systems, such as sensors, robotics, and smart logistics, to boost workflow efficiency and ensure consistent product quality.

title: Digital twin in design architecture: Impact of DT in architectural design for improved building lifecycle management
summary: Digital twins (DTs) are increasingly transforming the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry by enhancing data integration, visualization, collaboration, and decision-making throughout the building lifecycle. Despite these advances, limited research has examined the role of DTs in supporting architectural design for improved Building Lifecycle Management (BLM), particularly during the early design stages. This study investigates the potential of DT technology to enhance BLM by integrating digital twin concepts into the architectural design process. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining a comprehensive literature review with a questionnaire survey of 60 architecture, engineering, and construction professionals from Saudi Arabia, Nigeria, and the United States to evaluate current awareness, perceived benefits, implementation challenges, and opportunities associated with DT adoption. The findings indicate that while awareness of DT technology is increasing, its application to architectural design for comprehensive BLM remains limited. The study identifies key opportunities for improving decision-making, sustainability, lifecycle performance, and stakeholder collaboration, while highlighting workforce skills, interoperability, and implementation complexity as major barriers to adoption. By integrating literature-based evidence with industry perspectives, the research clarifies how design-stage decisions, digital information, and lifecycle requirements can be connected more effectively through DT-enabled processes. The findings further emphasize the importance of early planning for data integration, sensing requirements, performance evaluation, and interdisciplinary coordination. The study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital twin applications in architectural design by providing an evidence-based assessment of current adoption, opportunities, and challenges, offering practical insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers seeking to advance Building Lifecycle Management through digital transformation.

title: Navigating the digital frontier: unveiling the critical thresholds and strategic conditions for innovation performance in healthcare organizations
summary: Purpose This research aims to examine the effects of digital technology integration, dynamic capabilities and technological orientation on the innovation performance of China’s healthcare organizations. Design/methodology/approach Based on the dynamic capabilities view, this research employs a methodological triangulation approach, using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) and necessary condition analysis (NCA) to investigate how these digital change drivers interact. Findings The PLS-SEM findings reveal robust, positive interactions between technology integration, digital dynamic capabilities and innovation performance. Furthermore, this study demonstrates that technological orientation moderates the interplay among technology integration, dynamic capabilities and innovation performance. This implies that a strategic emphasis on technology will likely yield more innovation performance. The results from fsQCA highlight the need for precise configurations and conditions that lead to fruitful digital transformation in healthcare, given the variability and complexity of these transformations. The NCA results also show the thresholds and requirements for maximum digital integration in the healthcare industry. Originality/value The study contributes by examining how digital technology integration, digital dynamic capabilities and technological orientation jointly influence digital innovation performance. Its originality lies in the combined use of PLS-SEM, fsQCA and NCA to capture linear, configurational and threshold effects. While it extends existing frameworks rather than introducing new theory, the focus on healthcare organizations in China provides valuable contextual insight.

title: Exploring the relationships between successful implementation drivers of Quality 4.0: evidence from developing countries
summary: Purpose Digital transformation and automation are fundamental components of Quality 4.0, providing organizations with a strategic advantage by enhancing customer satisfaction and improving financial performance. The primary objective of this study is to identify the key drivers of Quality 4.0 implementation, evaluate their interrelationships using the decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory (DEMATEL) method and prioritize these drivers based on their significance and impact. A quantitative research approach is adopted to examine the determinants of organizational readiness for Quality 4.0 implementation in the manufacturing sectors of Iran and Malaysia. Design/methodology/approach This study investigates the critical determinants required for successful Quality 4.0 implementation in Iranian and Malaysian manufacturing industries and enables a comparative analysis using the DEMATEL methodology to identify the most and least influential indicators. Data were collected through purposive sampling from 14 experts representing diverse manufacturing industries. Findings The results indicate that big data, analytics, integrated management systems, vision and strategy, leadership, training, organizational culture and collaboration are the key drivers of successful Quality 4.0 implementation. The research follows a three-step methodology: (1) identification of relevant criteria through an extensive literature review, (2) validation of these criteria using the content validity ratio method and (3) application of the DEMATEL technique to analyze causal relationships and rank the drivers. Originality/value The DEMATEL analysis reveals that integrated management systems are the most influential and critical factor for the successful implementation of Quality 4.0, highlighting their central role in strengthening other organizational drivers, particularly in the context of developing countries.

title: A MODERATING EFFECT OF INFLATION ON THE IMPACT OF BOARD STRUCTURE ON THE FINANCIAL RESILIENCE OF ZOMBIE FIRMS IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA
summary: This study examines how inflation moderates the relationship between board structure—specifically, board gender diversity (BGD) and board financial expertise (BFE)—and the financial resilience of zombie firms in Nigeria. Board gender diversity and board financial expertise are considered determining factors for firm resilience. The research uses an ex-post facto design. It analyses panel data from 20 listed manufacturing firms identified as zombies, which had negative interest coverage ratios for three consecutive years between 2015 and 2024. Financial resilience is assessed using the Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio. Moderated regression analysis tests whether the effect of board structure on resilience changes with inflation. Findings show that the board structure's impact on financial resilience is significantly influenced by the macroeconomic environment, particularly by inflation. Board gender diversity is directly associated with a lower P/E ratio. When inflation is high, this relationship becomes positive. The effectiveness of gender diversity increases as inflation rises (β = 0.273, p = 0.028). In contrast, board financial expertise is positively linked to resilience under normal conditions. However, its beneficial effect weakens as inflation increases (β = -0.148, p = 0.089). The regression model is significant (F-statistic = 2.171, p = 0.042), accounting for about 11.9% of the variance in P/E ratios. These results indicate that the effectiveness of board attributes in promoting resilience depends on the inflationary context. The study highlights that governance does not universally improve firm resilience. It stresses the importance of tailoring board composition to economic conditions. These insights contribute to contingency and resource dependence theories, illustrating that the value of board resources varies with external conditions. The study offers recommendations for boards, investors, and policymakers to improve governance and resilience in inflation-prone markets.

title: LAW AT THE GREEN–DIGITAL FRONTIER: Reimagining Ecological Justice, Sustainability, Economics and Technology in Emerging Environmental Governance
summary: Environmental governance is changing fast. Problems in the natural world keep growing. At the same time, money needs and new technology are moving ahead. In this space, environmental law is not only about traditional regulation but it also touches sustainability goals, fairness for affected communities, trade-offs tied to the economy, and fresh technology methods. This includes artificial intelligence, remote sensing, satellite-based monitoring, blockchain, and systems that use environmental data to guide decisions. In that view, law, the economy, ecology, and technology must connect and work at the same time. It then looks at new legal areas that could support fresh ideas. The goal is to encourage change without harming nature. It also aims to protect fair distribution and long-term sustainability. In the end, the paper imagines a legal system that can respond as things shift. It would guide both the green transition and the digital transition. At the same time, it keeps human rights, environmental protection, and accountability as key parts.

title: Accounting Information Entropy–Resilience Theory: A Dynamic Theory of Accounting Information Quality Under Economic Shocks
summary: Accounting information has traditionally been evaluated through relatively static concepts such as relevance, faithful representation, earnings quality, disclosure quality, information asymmetry, and value relevance. These perspectives have generated substantial advances in accounting research, yet they provide limited theoretical explanation of how the informational properties of accounting systems evolve when firms encounter economic disturbances. This paper develops the Accounting Information Entropy–Resilience Theory (AIERT), a dynamic theoretical framework in which accounting information quality is conceptualized as a changing informational state rather than a fixed firm characteristic. The theory introduces two central constructs: Accounting Information Entropy, representing the degree of uncertainty, disorder, ambiguity, inconsistency, and informational instability contained in an accounting information environment; and Accounting Information Resilience, representing the capacity of that environment to resist, absorb, adapt to, and recover from disturbances while preserving economically useful information. The framework integrates information theory, accounting information economics, organizational resilience, dynamic capabilities, market microstructure, and economic decision theory. AIERT proposes that economic shocks can increase accounting information entropy, that entropy can exhibit persistence and nonlinear escalation, and that resilience determines the extent to which informational deterioration is absorbed or transmitted into economic decisions. The theory introduces resistance, recovery speed, recovery completeness, entropy persistence, critical entropy thresholds, hysteresis, informational equilibrium, and shock-amplification mechanisms. A dynamic state-space representation is developed to formalize these relationships. The paper advances seven theoretical propositions concerning shock sensitivity, resilience, nonlinear entropy dynamics, threshold behavior, recovery asymmetry, hysteresis, and economic consequences. It further distinguishes accounting information quality from accounting information resilience and argues that a high-quality information system in normal conditions may nevertheless exhibit low resilience under severe disturbance. The paper concludes by developing an empirical research agenda capable of testing AIERT and by outlining implications for accounting research, standard setting, auditing, corporate governance, investors, and economic policy.

title: Digital Transformation of the Procurement Function and Sustainable Performance of Private Logistics and Warehousing Firms in Nairobi County, Kenya.
summary: Digital transformation has become a strategic imperative in modern organizations, particularly within procurement functions, where the integration of digital tools, data systems and agile processes enhances efficiency, transparency and accountability. In Kenya, procurement accounts for about 10–13% of GDP, yet although more than 80% of public entities have implemented platforms such as IFMIS, only about 52% use them consistently, and logistics and warehousing firms continue to face low system utilization, inadequate technical skills, unreliable infrastructure and weak alignment between digital strategies and procurement objectives. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the influence of digital transformation of the procurement function on sustainable performance of private logistics and warehousing firms in Nairobi County, Kenya. It specifically examined the effects of digital strategy alignment, technological capabilities, data-driven proficiency and process agility on sustainable procurement performance. The study was anchored on the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Technology Acceptance Model and Institutional Theory. A descriptive and explanatory research design was adopted, targeting 1,250 active logistics and warehousing firms in Nairobi County, with procurement officers, supply chain managers, ICT personnel and operations managers as the units of observation. A sample of 93 firms was determined using Nassiuma's formula and selected through purposive and stratified sampling, with one respondent per firm. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire, and both descriptive and inferential statistical methods, namely Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis, were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four dimensions of digital transformation jointly explained 46.5% of the variation in sustainable procurement performance. Technological capabilities had the strongest positive and significant effect, followed by data-driven proficiency and digital strategy alignment, while process agility had a positive and significant but comparatively modest effect. The study, therefore, recommends that firms should upgrade ICT infrastructure and strengthen system integration and platform reliability, invest in analytics tools and staff training in procurement analytics, fully integrate procurement policies with digital transformation frameworks, and streamline procurement workflows to eliminate task duplication, so as to enhance sustainable procurement performance in logistics and warehousing firms in Nairobi County.

title: Inhibiting factors in digital supply chain implementation: Technology, organization, and environment framework study of the stilt-house industry in Tomohon City
summary: Digital transformation has reshaped supply chain management, yet adoption among small, traditional enterprises remains uneven. This study analyzes the factors inhibiting Digital Supply Chain (DSC) implementation among stilt-house (rumah panggung) producers in Tomohon City, a wood-based craft industry of cultural significance in North Sulawesi. A qualitative exploratory case study was analyzed through the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework. Data came from eight informants (four owners, two employees, one timber supplier, one customer), selected purposively, through participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation, and were analyzed with the Miles–Huberman–Saldaña interactive model, with source and technique triangulation. DSC implementation remains simple and not integrated: electric machinery in production, smartphones in marketing, and phone calls and WhatsApp in procurement operate as isolated applications. Barriers appear in all three TOE contexts: cost, limited electrical infrastructure, and unavailable equipment (technology); comfort with conventional systems despite adequate basic competence (organization); and supplier distance and unmet expectations of government support (environment). Informants consistently reported benefits from the technology in use, so barriers constrain the depth and integration of adoption rather than negate its value. The case also suggests, as an interpretation, that some manual work (e.g., hand-carving) persists as valued craft practice rather than an unmet digital need, qualifying deficit-based readings of traditional industries.

title: Absolute Environmental Sustainability Assessment of an Avocado Oil Supply Chain
summary: The increasing demand for avocado oil raises the question of whether production and consumption remain within environmentally sustainable limits. This study evaluated a cradle-to-grave avocado oil supply chain, produced in Colombia and consumed in Germany, by integrating Life Cycle Assessment with planetary-boundary-derived environmental budgets. The production and consumption of 1 kg of avocado oil generated 7.13 kg CO2-eq, 0.0074 kg P-eq, 0.0068 kg N-eq, 0.1875 m2·a crop-eq, and 1.95 m3 world-eq deprived for climate change, freshwater eutrophication, marine eutrophication, land use, and water use, respectively. Monte Carlo analysis (1000 iterations) indicated that the LCIA results were relatively stable with respect to the inventory uncertainty represented in the background data. We compared the environmental impacts associated with a hypothetical annual intake scenario in which the EAT–Lancet recommended intake of unsaturated oils is supplied entirely by avocado oil with allocated Safe Operating Space budgets. Under equal per-capita sharing, the per-person environmental entitlement is identical across geographical perspectives; geographical differentiation arises only when region-specific sharing factors, such as the economic/FCE factor, are applied. The results show that sustainability conclusions depend strongly on the principle used to share the available environmental capacity among products and activities.

title: Influence of Digital Planning Tools on Monitoring & Evaluation Frameworks at CHANCEN International, Rwanda
summary: Abstract: The adoption of digital technologies has transformed project management and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) practices by improving accountability, transparency, data quality, reporting efficiency, and evidence-based decision-making. This study examined the influence of digital planning tools on Monitoring and Evaluation frameworks at Chancen International Rwanda. Specifically, it assessed the influence of digital planning, budgeting, monitoring, and communication tools on the effectiveness of M&E frameworks. The study was guided by Contingency Theory, Modernization Theory, Cybernetics Theory, and Knowledge Management Theory. A mixed-methods research design was adopted, integrating quantitative and qualitative approaches. Quantitative data were collected from 359 respondents comprising staff, students, graduates, and partner institutions using simple random and census sampling techniques, while qualitative data were obtained through key informant interviews and documentary review. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and ANOVA in SPSS Version 26, whereas qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The findings revealed that digital planning tools significantly improved project scheduling, work-plan development, resource allocation, activity coordination, and strategic planning, thereby strengthening M&E frameworks. Digital budgeting tools enhanced budget preparation, financial tracking, cost control, resource utilization, and financial accountability, contributing to effective M&E implementation. Digital monitoring tools, including Kobo Toolbox, improved the timeliness, completeness, accuracy, and reliability of monitoring data while facilitating real-time reporting and performance tracking. Digital communication tools, including Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, and Looker Studio, enhanced information sharing, stakeholder engagement, dashboard visualization, report generation, feedback mechanisms, and evidence-based decision-making. Correlation analysis indicated significant positive relationships between all four categories of digital tools and M&E frameworks. Multiple regression analysis established that digital planning, budgeting, monitoring, and communication tools each had a statistically significant positive influence on M&E frameworks (p < 0.05), with digital communication tools emerging as the strongest predictor, followed by digital monitoring, budgeting, and planning tools. Collectively, these digital tools enhanced accountability, transparency, reporting timeliness, data quality, stakeholder participation, organizational learning, and evidence-based decision-making. The study concludes that integrating digital planning tools with complementary digital budgeting, monitoring, and communication technologies significantly strengthens Monitoring and Evaluation frameworks and organizational performance. It recommends increased investment in integrated digital M&E systems, continuous staff capacity building, strengthened digital infrastructure, centralized data management systems, and supportive digital transformation policies. title: Mekanisme Tata Kelola terhadap Kualitas Laba: Peran Moderasi Kecepatan Publikasi Laporan Keuangan
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of audit committee independence and external audit quality on earnings quality, with financial statement publication speed as both a direct variable and a moderating variable. Earnings quality is measured using discretionary accruals via the Modified Jones Model. Using a quantitative causal design and purposive sampling, 15 mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2025 were selected, yielding 75 observation data points. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model (REM) and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) in EViews. The empirical findings show that audit committee independence and external audit quality do not have a significant direct impact on earnings quality, indicating that internal governance structures and audit firm reputation often operate merely as regulatory compliance. Conversely, publication speed positively and significantly affects earnings quality, supporting signaling theory that timely financial reporting conveys transparent operational information. Furthermore, publication speed does not moderate the impact of audit committee independence on earnings quality, but it significantly weakens the relationship between external audit quality and earnings quality. This indicates that excessive time-budget pressure arising from accelerated publication deadlines compromises audit thoroughness, thereby diminishing audit quality effectiveness in curbing earnings management.

title: CORPORATE STRATEGY TO HUMAN CAPITAL: THE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE TRANSITION IN HOSPITALITY WITH A BIBLIOMETRIC APPROACH
summary: Within The Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework has become a defining paradigm in the transformation of the hospitality industry, shifting the focus from profit-oriented models to integrated sustainability and accountability systems. In this context, understanding how ESG research evolves and what dimensions dominate the discourse becomes increasingly important. The aim of this study is to analyse the development of ESG-related research in hospitality between 2009 and 2025, with particular attention to the transition from financial governance to human capital-oriented approaches. Despite the expansion of the field, the literature remains fragmented, characterised by conceptual ambiguity with Corporate Social Responsibility, inconsistent measurement practices, and limited integration of ESG dimensions within servicebased industries. The research is based on a bibliometric analysis of 987 publications indexed in the Web of Science database. The methodological approach combines performance analysis with science mapping techniques in order to identify publication trends, intellectual structures, and conceptual developments within the field. The results indicate a significant increase in research activity after 2019, accompanied by a shift in thematic focus. Earlier studies primarily emphasised financial performance, environmental efficiency, and external stakeholder perceptions. In contrast, recent research highlights the growing importance of employees as key drivers of ESG value creation. This reflects a redefinition of the Social dimension, which increasingly functions as an internal governance mechanism centred on employee engagement, well-being, and organisational behaviour. At the same time, the Environmental and Governance dimensions remain strongly interconnected through performance metrics and regulatory requirements, resulting in an imbalanced ESG structure. The internal social dimension is less standardised and insufficiently integrated into strategic decision-making processes. The study concludes that this imbalance limits the effectiveness of ESG implementation in the hospitality sector. The findings suggest that future development depends on the systematic integration of human capital considerations into governance frameworks, particularly in response to emerging European sustainability regulations. The contribution of the paper lies in identifying the internal social dimension as a key frontier of ESG research and in providing a structured overview of the field’s evolution, offering both theoretical clarification and practical relevance for sustainability-oriented management in hospitality.

title: A resource-based strategic management in Sharia banks: Examining the association of organizational culture, innovation, and digital transformation
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractSharia banking institutions in Indonesia have significant growth potential, given that the majority of the population is Muslim. This study aims to analyze the association between organizational culture, innovation, and digital transformation within the context of resource-based strategic management in Sharia banks of East Java. Data were collected from state-owned (6 main and 90 branch offices) and private (3 main and 66 branch offices) Sharia banks in East Java during January and February 2026, after these Sharia banks completed their annual financial reports. A total of 165 respondents were selected using a purposive sampling method. The selected respondents were secretaries with at least three years of work experience. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling partial least squares (SEM-PLS). The analysis results show that organizational culture has a positive and significant relationship with resource-based strategic management (path coefficient = 0.450; t = 8.640; p < 0.001). Innovation also has a positive and significant relationship with resource-based strategic management (path coefficient = 0.305; t = 5.742; p < 0.001). Similarly, digital transformation has a positive and significant relationship with resource-based strategic management (path coefficient = 0.349; t = 6.183; p < 0.001). These findings indicate that organizational culture, innovation, and digital transformation are positively related to resource-based strategic management in Sharia banks of East Java.

title: LABOR MARKET SEGMENTATION IN THE CONTEXT OF THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF THE ECONOMY
summary: This article examines current trends in labor market segmentation in the context of the digital transformation of the economy. It explores the main criteria for labor market segmentation, the characteristics of internal and external labor markets, as well as the impact of digitalization and platform employment on the employment structure. The paper analyzes labor shortages, skill mismatches, and regional disparities. Particular attention is paid to the development of digital forms of employment, changing requirements for workers' professional competencies, and the transformation of labor relations. The article highlights the need to improve public policy in the field of labor market regulation, human capital development, and the adaptation of the vocational education and training system to current economic conditions.

title: Pengaruh Ukuran Perusahaan, Ukuran Kantor Akuntan Publik (KAP) dan Profitabilitas terhadap Audit Delay pada Emiten LQ45 yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Tahun 2023 – 2024
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of company size, Public Accounting Firm size, and profitability on audit delay in companies listed in the LQ45 index on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2023–2024 period. The research method used is a quantitative approach with a purposive sampling technique, resulting in 90 observations from audited financial statements. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the classical assumption test. The results of the study indicate that company size and Public Accounting Firm size negatively and significantly affect audit delay. This means that the larger the company size and if the company is audited by a Public Accounting Firm affiliated with the Big Four, the shorter the audit delay time will be. However, profitability does not affect audit delay. This finding provides implications for companies with high or low profitability values to still go through the audit process in accordance with applicable provisions. This study contributes recent empirical evidence from LQ45 issuers for 2023–2024, showing that audit delay is more closely associated with firm size and public accounting firm size than with profitability, thereby enriching evidence on the determinants of audit timeliness in the Indonesian capital market. Keywords: audit delay, company size, public accounting firm size, profitability, LQ45

title: Pengaruh Inventory Intensity, Capital Intensity dan Corporate Governance terhadap Manajemen Pajak
summary: This study aims to determine the effect of *Inventory Intensity, Capital Intensity,* and *Corporate Governance*, proxied by Independent Commissioners, on tax management, both partially and simultaneously. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data in the form of financial statements of the companies selected as research objects. The sampling technique used is *purposive sampling*, which involves selecting samples based on predetermined criteria in accordance with the research objectives. The collected data were analyzed using EViews Version 12 through several statistical testing procedures to examine the relationships and effects between the independent and dependent variables. *Inventory Intensity* is used to measure the level of a company's investment in inventory, while *Capital Intensity* reflects the proportion of the company's investment in fixed assets. Meanwhile, *Corporate Governance* is proxied by Independent Commissioners as one of the company's monitoring mechanisms. The results show that *Inventory Intensity, Capital Intensity,* and *Corporate Governance* partially have an effect on tax management. The simultaneous test results also indicate that *Inventory Intensity, Capital Intensity,* and *Corporate Governance* collectively have an effect on tax management. These findings indicate that corporate decisions related to inventory, fixed assets, and corporate governance play an important role in determining a company's tax management strategies.

title: Digital Transformation and the Relationship between Service Users and Public Administration
summary: Abstract This study examines how service users perceptions of digital transformation, access to information and waiting times relate to their perceived relationship with public administration in Morocco. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire distributed via LinkedIn and in person at several public administrations. Of the 146 people who responded, the 122 with complete answers on the model variables were retained for the regression analysis, The 14 measurement items cover four constructs, whose factorability and internal consistency were checked with Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin and Bartlett tests and Cronbachs alpha 0.725 to 0.811. A multiple linear regression explains 55.3% of the variance in the perceived relationship “adjusted R² = 0.542”. Perceived digital transformation β = 0.475, p < 0.001 and perceived reduction in waiting times β = 0.245, p = 0.003 are positively and significantly associated with the outcome, whereas the coefficient for access to information is positive but not significant at the 5% level (β = 0.135, p = 0.074). For these respondents, the quality of the relationship with the administration appears to depend more on visible changes in how services are delivered, including the time they take, than on information alone. Because the design is cross-sectional and relies on self-reported perceptions, the findings describe associations rather than causal effects. title: Evaluating AI pilot zones’ impact on enterprise digital transformation: a quasi-natural experiment
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) pilot zones are place-based institutional innovations intended to integrate the digital and real economies. Using panel data for Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011–2023, this study estimates their effect on enterprise digital transformation with difference-in-differences (DID) methods. The baseline coefficient is 0.804, equivalent to 2.25% of the sample mean. The result is robust to sensitivity analysis, placebo tests, PSM-DID, counterfactual tests, competing-policy controls and the Sun–Abraham interaction-weighted estimator. Human-capital agglomeration and eased financing constraints are identified as key channels. Point estimates are larger in western regions, highly competitive industries and labour- or capital-intensive firms. The findings explain how phased regional AI policy shapes enterprise transformation and support differentiated policy design.

title: Pengaruh Ukuran Perusahaan, Leverage, dan Profitabilitas terhadap Manajemen Laba pada Perusahaan Pertambangan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Tahun 2022–2024
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of firm size, leverage, and profitability on earnings management in mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2022–2024 period. This study employs a quantitative approach with a causal-associative research design. The population consists of mining companies listed on the IDX. Based on purposive sampling, 45 companies were selected, resulting in 135 observations. The data consist of annual financial statements and were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS software. The results show that firm size has a significant negative effect on earnings management, while leverage and profitability have no significant effect. These findings indicate that larger companies have a lower tendency to engage in earnings management due to stricter oversight. The implications of this study are expected to provide consideration for management, investors, and regulators in improving transparency and strengthening financial reporting oversight.

title: ACCOUNTING CONSERVATISM AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF LISTED INDUSTRIAL GOODS FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examined the effect of accounting conservatism on the financial performance of listed industrial goods firms in Nigeria. Specifically, the study assessed the effects of earnings conservatism and balance sheet conservatism on Return on Assets (ROA) and Return on Equity (ROE). The study was anchored on Positive Accounting Theory and Agency Theory. An ex-post facto research design was adopted, while a quantitative panel data approach was employed. The population comprised listed industrial goods firms operating in Nigeria, from which firms with complete and relevant financial information for the period 2020–2024 were purposively selected. Secondary data were obtained from the audited annual financial statements of the selected firms. Descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis were employed to analyse the data and test the formulated hypotheses. The findings revealed that earnings conservatism had a positive and significant effect on ROA and ROE, while balance sheet conservatism also had a positive and significant effect on ROA and ROE. The regression models explained 55.1% of the variation in ROA and 61.0% of the variation in ROE, with both models being statistically significant. The study concludes that accounting conservatism is an important factor influencing the financial performance of manufacturing firms. It recommends that manufacturing firms strengthen prudent earnings recognition and balance sheet valuation practices, while regulatory authorities should enhance oversight and compliance with applicable financial reporting standards. Appropriate application of accounting conservatism is expected to improve the reliability of financial information, reduce information asymmetry, and enhance corporate financial performance

title: Pengaruh Leverage dan Profitabilitas terhadap Manajemen Laba pada Perusahaan Manufaktur di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: Earnings management is an important issue in financial reporting because it can reduce the quality of financial information used by investors, creditors, and other stakeholders in making decisions. Leverage and profitability are frequently examined as factors that may influence management’s tendency to engage in earnings management. However, previous studies have reported inconsistent findings. This study aims to examine the effect of leverage and profitability on earnings management in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange through a literature review approach. The study reviews scholarly articles obtained from Google Scholar and published between 2024 and 2026. Articles were selected using purposive sampling based on inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in 31 articles for analysis. Data were analyzed using content analysis by comparing previous findings to identify patterns, inconsistencies, and research gaps. The results show that the effect of leverage on earnings management remains inconsistent, with studies reporting positive, negative, and insignificant effects. Profitability also produces mixed findings, although most studies indicate a positive relationship with earnings management. These differences may be attributed to variations in research objects, observation periods, measurement proxies, and analytical methods. This study provides an overview of previous findings and identifies research gaps for future research.

title: Supply chain risk identification using AI-powered topic modelling: implications for demand forecasting in oil and gas companies
summary: The oil and gas industry is highly exposed to political, economic, and supply–demand disruptions, making early risk identification critical for supply chain performance. This study applies AI-enabled topic modelling to extract risk indicators from large unstructured datasets and integrates them into gasoline demand forecasting models, showing how qualitative risk signals can improve uncertainty management in supply chains. Building on these insights, the paper proposes a generalisable three-stage methodological framework that formalises the pipeline from automated text-based risk identification through forecast validation to short-term operational adjustment. In this context, short-term operational adjustments include tactical changes to procurement, inventory levels, production scheduling, logistics routeing, and short-term hedging decisions made in response to risk-aware demand and volatility forecasts. The framework’s principal methodological contribution lies in operationalising AI-enabled text analytics within real-world supply chain planning processes through a formally specified decision-flow model. Results from the empirical validation on a 15-year gasoline demand dataset show that incorporating text-derived risk indicators, selected via rigorous feature selection, improves both point-forecast accuracy and density-forecast calibration relative to naive and seasonal baselines, offering transferable guidance for policymakers and industry stakeholders seeking to strengthen energy system resilience.

title: ECONOMETRIC ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL ECONOMY DEVELOPMENT ON ECONOMIC GROWTH IN UZBEKISTAN
summary: This study empirically examines the impact of digital economy development on economic growth in Uzbekistan using annual time-series data from 2000 to 2023. Given the rapid structural transition of the Uzbek economy, the research evaluates whether consumer digital adoption (internet penetration and mobile cellular subscriptions) has yielded statistically significant short-term macroeconomic returns. Preliminary Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) unit root testing revealed severe nonstationarity in physical capital formation (>I(2)), explicitly invalidating standard cointegration techniques such as ARDL bounds testing.

title: Drone technology in medical supply chain management: A survey on enabling technologies, frameworks, and applications
summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), or drones, have become known as a disruptive technology that can potentially enhance efficiency and accessibility in the medical supply chain by allowing the timely delivery of medical supplies such as vaccines, blood, organs and emergency drugs in remote and disaster-prone regions. This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of existing international research on the use of drones in medical supply chains, with a sample of 1,209 articles retrieved from the Dimensions.ai database for 2015-2026. VOSviewer was used to process the bibliographic information to determine publication growth and trends, leading authors and journals, country contributions and collaboration patterns, while a thematic analysis was conducted to identify the major and emerging research themes. The findings indicate that the past few years have witnessed a significant increase in the number of publications, which signifies increased interest in UAVs in healthcare supply chains, and that the most important research themes are emergency medical transportation, vaccine delivery, last-mile delivery of health care and drone system efficiency. In addition, a country-by-country examination reveals that the United States is at the forefront. Overall, the study provides information about recent trends and future perspectives on capitalizing on drone technology in medical supply chains.

title: The Effect of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Disclosure, Environmental Performance, And Environmental Cost on Financial Performance (Empirical Study on Industrials Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the Period 2020–2025)
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosure, Environmental Performance, and Environmental Cost on Financial Performance in Industrials Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the Period 2020–2025. The research sample was determined using a purposive sampling method, resulting in 10 companies observed over 6 years, producing an initial 60 firm-year observations, of which 3 were identified as outliers, leaving a final sample of 57 observations. The dependent variable, Financial Performance, is proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), while Environmental Performance is measured using the PROPER rating, Environmental Cost is measured as the ratio of total environmental costs to net income after tax, and CSR disclosure is measured using the Corporate Social Responsibility Disclosure Index (CSRDI) based on GRI indicators. Hypothesis testing was conducted using multiple linear regression analysis with the assistance of SPSS 29 software. The results indicate that CSR disclosure has a positive and significant effect on Financial Performance (β = 0.325; sig. = 0.021), Environmental Performance has a positive and significant effect on Financial Performance (β = 0.291; sig. = 0.018), while Environmental Cost has no significant effect on Financial Performance (β = 0.243; sig. = 0.184). Simultaneously, the three independent variables significantly affect Financial Performance (F = 6.328; sig. < 0.001), with the model explaining 38.6% of the variation in ROA (Adjusted R² = 0.386)

title: Mekari Jurnal: Accounting Software Utilizing AI Technology
summary: Mekari Jurnal is a cloud-based accounting and financial management software platform that utilizes artificial intelligence (AI) technology to help businesses manage their financial processes in an integrated system. The use of AI in accounting software can support process automation, data processing, and more efficient access to financial information. As an accounting software platform, Mekari Jurnal supports a wide range of business financial management needs. Its capabilities cover bookkeeping, transaction recording, invoicing and accounts receivable, expense tracking, inventory management, bank reconciliation, taxation, and financial reporting. Through automation and data integration, Mekari Jurnal helps reduce manual bookkeeping tasks while providing businesses with better visibility into their financial condition. The use of AI technology also supports the development of more efficient approaches to accounting processes and financial data management. The platform serves businesses of different sizes and industries in Indonesia that need a more structured, integrated, and data-driven approach to financial management. AI Technology in Accounting Software Advances in AI are expanding the role of accounting software beyond transaction recording and financial reporting. AI technology can support repetitive task automation, large-scale data processing, and the analysis of financial information. In this context, Mekari Jurnal utilizes AI technology as part of its accounting software solutions to support business accounting processes and financial data management. By combining accounting software with AI technology, the platform reflects how digital tools can help businesses manage financial workflows more efficiently. Mekari Jurnal's Capabilities Mekari Jurnal helps businesses manage various financial activities through a single platform, allowing information from different processes to be organized and accessed more systematically. Its capabilities include: - Bookkeeping and transaction recording - Invoicing and accounts receivable management - Expense tracking and monitoring - Inventory management - Bank reconciliation - Tax management - Financial reporting - Automation and data processing to support accounting workflows These capabilities help businesses reduce reliance on manual processes and monitor financial information more easily. title: Climate governance as a determinant of climate change disclosure quality: Evidence from African listed firms
summary: Climate change disclosure quality is important for assessing how firms identify, manage, and communicate climate-related risks and opportunities, yet evidence on governance mechanisms that support high-quality disclosure remains limited in African capital markets. This study examines the effect of climate governance on climate change disclosure quality among listed firms in nine African countries. Guided by the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) framework, disclosure quality is measured using a weighted index of eleven TCFD-aligned disclosures. Climate governance is measured using a composite index of risk management, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), and environmental committees, together with executive climate incentives. Data for 137 firms from 2017 to 2025 were collected through content analysis and structured into an unbalanced panel that was analysed using the two-step System Generalised Method of Moments estimator. The results show that climate governance improves disclosure quality. Further analysis shows that CSR and environmental committees improve disclosure quality, while similar evidence is not established for risk management committees and executive climate incentives. The study contributes evidence on the collective and individual effects of climate governance on TCFD-aligned disclosure quality in a climate-vulnerable African context. The findings highlight the importance of strengthening climate governance structures to support higher-quality disclosure.

title: The Digital Lever: How Can Digital Intelligence Transformation Drive Urban Green Innovation?
summary: The digital and intelligent transformation of urban development has sparked new reflections on green innovation in cities for the new era. China’s national big data comprehensive pilot zone policy provides a practical arena for exploring this issue. This study, based on panel data from 287 prefecture-level cities in China from 2011 to 2022, examines the mechanisms through which the national big data comprehensive pilot zone policy affects urban green innovation. The results show that the pilot zone policy significantly improves the level of urban green innovation, with the level of digital economic development and the intensity of environmental regulation being important mediating pathways, forming a dual path of technology-driven and institutional synergy. Based on the empirical analysis results, the study proposes a “digital lever” framework to explain the combined effects of policy foundations, digital empowerment, and environmental regulation.

title: The Dual Synergistic Effect of Digital Policies: How Data Factorization and Technological Intelligence Co‐Shape Corporate ESG Performance
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how the synergy between data factorization and technological intelligence affects corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance using comprehensive panel data from Chinese A‐share listed companies (2007–2024). Leveraging the staggered establishment of National Big Data Comprehensive Pilot Zones and National Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Application Pilot Zones as a well‐identified quasi‐natural experiment, we provide causal evidence that policy synergy significantly enhances corporate ESG performance, with this composite effect notably surpassing any single‐dimensional pilot policy. Net effect tests further reveal that while building artificial intelligence upon an established big data foundation yields a significant marginal premium over isolated AI policies, this synergistic dividend is not instantaneous. Mechanism tests reveal that the policy synergy improves corporate ESG performance through two core channels: the technology empowerment effect and the governance optimization effect. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that policy synergy effects are more pronounced in domestic enterprises, core digital economy industries, and nonheavily polluting sectors. Additionally, the transmission efficiency of policy dividends is positively moderated by favorable internal resource endowments and external institutional pressures yet inhibited by severe financial constraints. Further analysis demonstrates an optimal temporal sequencing pattern consistent with dynamic complementarity theory: following a “factor accumulation first, intelligent application second” implementation logic, with synergy dividends peaking when artificial intelligence policies supplement big data policies after approximately 3 years. This study advances the literature by moving beyond single‐policy evaluation to identify the causal effects and temporal laws of policy complementarity, revealing the micromechanism of digital policy synergy driving corporate value creation and providing important empirical support for government optimization of the temporal sequencing and spatial layout of digital economy governance systems.

title: Generative AI risk prediction capability and cross border agricultural trade resilience: a PLS-SEM empirical study of coastal Chinese enterprises
summary: Introduction Maritime transport carries the predominant share of cross-border agricultural trade, and geopolitical conflicts, climate anomalies, port congestion, and proliferating trade barriers have intensified uncertainty for the coastal enterprises that depend on seaborne logistics. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new pathways for building resilient supply chains through multi-source data fusion and risk prediction capabilities. However, empirical evidence examining how GenAI risk prediction capability (GenAI-RPC) relates to cross-border agricultural trade resilience (CATR) remains scarce. Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV) and dynamic capability theory, this study develops a direct-effects model linking three GenAI-RPC dimensions---multi-source cross-border risk identification and scoring, prediction accuracy and anti-hallucination stability, and AI risk model calibration and decision empowerment---to CATR. Methods Using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), we analyzed survey data from 300 agricultural enterprises engaged in cross-border trade across four coastal Chinese provinces (Shandong, Guangdong, Fujian, and Zhejiang). Results The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity: Cronbach's α ranged from 0.817 to 0.855, composite reliability from 0.880 to 0.902, and average variance extracted (AVE) from 0.623 to 0.697. All heterotrait-monotrait (HTMT) ratios were below 0.85, supporting discriminant validity. The structural model showed that all three GenAI-RPC dimensions were positively associated with CATR: multi-source risk identification ( β = 0.291, p < 0.001), prediction accuracy ( β = 0.251, p < 0.001), and model calibration ( β = 0.287, p < 0.001). The model explained 46.1% of the variance in CATR ( R 2 = 0.461; Stone--Geisser Q 2 = 0.112), with SRMR = 0.069 indicating acceptable fit. Among the control variables, enterprise digital transformation maturity showed a strong positive association with CATR ( β = 0.577, p < 0.001), and all three GenAI-RPC dimensions remained statistically significant after controlling for it. Discussion These findings contribute to the theoretical integration of GenAI capabilities with maritime supply chain resilience research and offer practical guidance for coastal agricultural enterprises and policymakers seeking to strengthen the resilience of seaborne food trade.

title: Drug shortages in Italy: strategic insights and empirical evidence from the Italian pharmaceutical market
summary: Abstract Drug shortages disrupt healthcare delivery and pose a critical challenge to the resilience of pharmaceutical supply chains. This study investigates the drivers of drug shortages in Italy – Europe’s leading pharmaceutical producer – to identify the factors associated with supply disruptions and inform evidence-based health policy. Using national data from 2018 to 2023, we analysed 17,619 drugs across 3,013 groups of substitutes, covering community , dual-dispensed , and hospital distribution channels. Generalised linear mixed models were employed to assess how drug characteristics, market dynamics, and regulatory features influence shortage risk. Shortages were most prevalent among community drugs, where high market fragmentation and low-profit margins contributed to supply instability. Patent protection was associated with lower shortage risk for non-sterile drugs, while sterile drugs remained vulnerable regardless of patent status, likely due to manufacturing complexity. Notably, price effects were age-dependent: higher prices mitigated shortage risk, particularly for older drugs. This study offers a comprehensive evaluation of shortage patterns in a key pharmaceutical market, identifying structural risk factors and market vulnerabilities. The findings provide actionable insights for policymakers aiming to design targeted interventions, strengthen supply chain resilience, and ensure continuous access to essential medicines.

title: Accounting and Maritime Accounting: Differences and Relationships
summary: Background: The global and Indonesian maritime sector requires accounting systems capable of addressing distinctive transaction characteristics, operational risks, and sustainability demands. Maritime accounting refers to accounting practices adapted to shipping, port, marine, and fisheries industries. However, its conceptual boundaries and scope remain insufficiently defined in the literature. Objective: This study aims to analyze the differences and relationships between general and maritime accounting, identify the principal dimensions distinguishing the two concepts, and propose a conceptual framework positioning maritime accounting within the broader accounting discipline. Methods: This study employed an integrative literature review. A total of 45 articles were identified from Google Scholar and Garuda (Garba Rujukan Digital) using keywords related to maritime accounting and the blue economy. After screening based on relevance, methodological rigor, and publication within the last five years, 25 articles were selected for thematic analysis. Results: The findings indicate that maritime accounting differs from general accounting in terms of recording objects and asset characteristics, cost and revenue structures, operational and environmental risk management, and the integration of environmental and sustainability aspects through the blue accounting approach. Operational complexity and sustainability integration emerged as the most distinctive characteristics. Nevertheless, maritime accounting remains fundamentally grounded in the principles of general accounting, while adapting their application to the specific characteristics of maritime industries. Conclusion: Maritime accounting represents a sectoral specialization that extends the role of accounting in supporting sustainable maritime economic development. The proposed conceptual framework provides a foundation for future empirical research and the development of accounting standards relevant to maritime industries.

title: Economic Profitability of ESG Investments in the Wine Sector: A Bibliometric Systematic Literature Review
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether and under which conditions ESG investments are associated with profitability in the wine sector. A PRISMA‐guided bibliometric–systematic review of 83 peer‐reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science combines bibliometric mapping, qualitative synthesis, and MMAT‐based quality appraisal. ESG investments do not generate uniform returns. Profitability emerges when firms transform sustainability investments into organizational capabilities and stakeholders recognize and reward the resulting value, a process shaped by internal, external, and temporal boundary conditions. Wineries should tailor ESG strategies to their capabilities, market context, and time horizon, while policy support should address sector‐specific structural barriers. Integrating the Natural Resource‐Based View and Stakeholder Theory, the study proposes a unified framework explaining heterogeneous ESG–profitability outcomes. However, the evidence base is predominantly environmental, limiting conclusions for social and governance dimensions.

title: Cost Stickiness and Opportunistic Insider Trading
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates whether cost management decisions are associated with insider trading profits. We hypothesize that prior to stock sales, self‐serving managers reduce costs to inflate earnings and boost stock prices, while before stock purchases, they maintain higher costs to depress earnings and lower stock prices. Such adjustments create asymmetry in cost behaviour, amplifying or dampening cost stickiness: the well‐documented tendency of costs to rise more with sales increases than they fall with sales decreases. Drawing on the classification method of Cohen et al., we separate opportunistic from routine insider trades. We find that cost stickiness decreases prior to opportunistic sales and increases before opportunistic purchases, with these results robust to multiple insider trade definitions and alternative measures of cost stickiness. Further analyses show that strong corporate governance weakens, while financial opacity intensifies the association between cost behaviour and insider trading gains. These effects are especially pronounced for trades executed by CEOs and CFOs. While our empirical approach documents robust correlations rather than definitive causal mechanisms, the results are consistent with the view that managers may utilize real cost adjustments alongside insider trading, extending prior studies focused primarily on accrual‐based adjustments. Collectively, the results highlight important patterns relevant to corporate governance, market participants, and regulators concerned with financial reporting integrity and insider trading practices.

title: Green intellectual capital and green performance in Islamic higher education: the mediating role of green innovation
summary: This study aims to explore the mediating role of Green Innovation on the relationship between Green Intellectual Capital and Green Performance in Islamic Higher Education. Primary data was collected through a questionnaire from leaders/strategic managers at Muhammadiyah and Aisyiyah Universities (PTMA). The number of respondents in this study was 313. Green Human Capital does not directly impact Green Performance. In other words, the existence of individual environmental knowledge and competencies does not automatically translate into institutional environmental performance. Meanwhile, Green Innovation does not mediate the relationship between Green Relational Capital and Green Performance. This means that external relations in the context of Islamic higher education are more legitimacy-driven than innovation-driven. This research provides a policy roadmap for IHE leaders to develop GICs. Furthermore, this research can guide resource allocation toward a portfolio of green innovations that directly improve cost efficiency and reduce emissions. The originality of this research lies in its contextualization within IHE, an ecosystem with a mandate for scientific and moral outreach, distinct from general universities and business entities. Furthermore, the operationalization of GI mediation in a campus setting is not merely an intervening variable, but rather a measurable, dynamic capability.

title: The nonlinear scale-matching mechanism of green innovation transfer: Insights from explainable machine learning
summary: Addressing climate change and advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) have positioned green innovation as a key driver of urban ecological transformation and regional competitiveness. Growing attention focuses on the mechanisms of green innovation transfer and diffusion among cities. Systematically uncovering patterns and mechanisms of green innovation collaboration across different city size combinations is crucial for understanding urban innovation network evolution and enhancing regional green innovation governance. Using data from 297 Chinese cities between 2001 and 2020, including intercity green patent transfers and other multi-source datasets, this study employs the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) machine learning model to systematically analyze the nonlinear effects of city size combinations on green innovation collaboration. The results indicate that China's Green Innovation Network (GIN) has evolved from concentration in core cities to a multi-centered, widely connected, and hierarchically coordinated structure. During this process, collaboration was influenced by nonlinear interactions of cities of different population sizes, exhibiting pronounced threshold stratification and staged transitions. Further analysis reveals that the optimal pairing patterns mainly involve diversified collaboration paths between medium-small and large cities, between medium-large and small cities, as well as between large city pairs. By contrast, the least favorable pairing occurs when the target city has a population between 1 and 3 million, a category that has long remained within a “low-efficiency cooperation zone.” This study enriches the theoretical framework of GIN and provides scientific evidence to support the optimization of regional green innovation policies and urban collaborative innovation strategies.

title: Digital Transformation in the Textile Cutting Sector: An Industry 4.0 Approach to Operational Excellence
summary: Purpose – This study investigates how the integration of Industry 4.0 monitoring technologies with structured change management and employee involvement can improve FCI system adoption, operational data quality, and warehouse efficiency in the cutting department of a Portuguese textile SME. Design/methodology/approach – Action research methodology was employed across four iterative phases – problem identification, action planning, implementation, and reflection – at ATêxteis S.A., a knitwear manufacturer. Data collection triangulated direct observation, FCI/ERP system logs, anonymous employee questionnaires, and supervisor interviews. Theoretical grounding draws on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Kotter’s eight-step change model. Findings – FCI system registrations increased nearly three-fold (300 to 1,000 per month) between November 2022 and July 2023, with registrations per 1,000 pieces cut rising from 3.5 to 12.2. Remnant warehouse occupancy decreased from 28.35% to approximately 15% of total capacity. ERP integration enabled automatic detection of material consumption discrepancies, and quality non-conformance detection increased from an estimated 5–8 to 23 cases per period. Results confirm that change management and participatory training are the proximate drivers of digital tool adoption, even when system use is formally mandated. Originality – The study provides rare empirical evidence on Industry 4.0 implementation in textile SME cutting operations, extending TAM and Kotter’s model to a manufacturing digitalization context. It introduces a production-normalized utilization metric (registrations per 1,000 pieces) and demonstrates the complementarity of Lean principles with digital monitoring for operational excellence in traditional manufacturing.
