title: Digital Transformation and Ecosystem Evolution of Kazakhstan’s Banks: An Integrative Review and Conceptual Model
summary: Purpose of the research. The purpose of this article is to synthesize and systematize existing knowledge on the ecosystem competitiveness of Kazakhstani banks in the context of their transition to digital ecosystembased models, as well as to develop a conceptual model. Methodology. The study employs an integrative literature review method based on methodological guidelines, using the Scopus, Google Scholar, and Dimensions databases for the period 2010–2025. The conceptual framework is built around the linkage between ecosystem maturity (EM), orchestration capabilities (OC), data governance quality and use (DGQ), the strength of the data–network–activity (DNA) cycle, and ecosystem-based competitiveness (EBC), with regulatory openness (RO), legacy burden, and BigTech pressure acting as moderating factors. Originality / Value of the research. This study contributes to a holistic understanding of how the transition of Kazakhstani banks to digital ecosystem models affects their competitiveness. Its theoretical contribution lies in identifying research directions for future empirical and conceptual studies. The practical significance is reflected in the formulation of recommendations for prioritizing API partnerships, managing data quality, and standardizing interfaces. Findings . The integrative literature review reveals that, in addition to the validated mechanisms EM→OC/ DGQ→DNA→EBC, the academic community is divided into two competing theoretical schools: (i) innovationoriented and (ii) institutional–regulatory. The review also enables the development of an integrated model of pathways to ecosystem competitiveness for banks in Kazakhstan. Within this model, ecosystem competitiveness is shaped through the interaction of (1) technological and platform maturity, (2) orchestration and analytical capabilities, including data management and the development of network effects, and (3) institutional and market conditions, primarily the regulatory environment and competitive pressure from BigTech firms. Positive ecosystem effects emerge only when these components develop in a coordinated manner.

title: Forensic Accounting and the Doctrine of Criminal Intent in Financial Fraud: A Legal and Audit-Based Examination of Mexico’s Oceanografía–Banamex Case
summary: Financial fraud in receivables financing presents challenges for identifying documentary manipulation, tracing financial responsibility, and assessing evidence of criminal intent. This study develops an integrated forensic accounting and legal assessment framework to examine Mexico’s Oceanografía–Banamex case, focusing on the relationship between financial irregularities, authorization practices, and evidence relevant to deliberate deception. The framework combines transaction reconstruction, invoice verification, documentary triangulation, transaction network analysis, and an evidence matrix to distinguish indicators of intentional misconduct from negligence and weaknesses in internal controls. The study dataset comprises 12,000 receivables financing records, 2,400 invoice documents, 180 authorization logs, and 60 correspondence files covering a three year observation period. Data preparation involves record standardization, duplicate identification, chronological alignment, and reconciliation of invoices with financing and approval information. Twenty four forensic indicators assess unsupported receivables, repeated invoices, inconsistent approval dates, unusual financing concentrations, documentary discrepancies, and authorization exceptions. Rule based screening and network analysis identify potentially irregular transactions, which are subsequently assessed against reference labels through independent documentary review. Legal analysis organizes the resulting evidence according to its relevance to knowledge, deception, participation, and financial benefit, while considering alternative explanations. The integrated framework identifies 912 of 960 labelled irregular records, achieving 95.0% recall. Among 1,000 flagged records, 912 correspond to reference irregularities, yielding 91.2% precision and a 93.1% F1 score. Conventional checklist screening identifies 720 irregular records, producing 75.0% recall. The proposed approach therefore improves recall by 20 percentage points, demonstrating stronger identification of irregular financing patterns within the analyzed dataset. Documentary inconsistencies and recurring authorization exceptions provide priorities for further investigation, although these indicators alone cannot establish criminal intent or individual guilt. The study contributes an auditable framework connecting financial analysis with legally relevant evidentiary assessment. Its findings support integrated verification, transaction tracing, and contextual review as complementary tools for investigating complex financial fraud. The framework emphasizes evidence provenance, document authentication, corroboration, and distinctions between suspicious transactions and established responsibility. Its practical value lies in strengthening investigative prioritization and audit transparency while supporting carefully qualified legal interpretation of financial evidence within the examined case context.

title: Hybrid multi-criteria decision-making and quantum-inspired metaheuristics for large-scale supply chain network optimisation
summary: Abstract Large-scale supply chain network (SCN) optimization faces significant challenges due to multi-objective trade-offs, dynamic demand patterns, and computational scalability issues. This paper proposes a hybrid optimisation framework that integrates quantum particle swarm optimisation (QPSO) with the fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (FAHP) to handle conflicting objectives, including cost minimisation, sustainability enhancement, and network resilience improvement. The framework incorporates a post-hoc explainability module based on Shapley value analysis, applied after QPSO convergence, providing interpretable insights into facility locations, product flows, and inventory decisions to support transparent stakeholder communication. The framework is evaluated on fifteen benchmark instances spanning 50 to 500 nodes, together with one anonymised industrial case study. Across the benchmark suite, the framework achieved an average cost reduction of 12.4%, an average sustainability improvement of 18.3%, and an average social-impact improvement of 14.6% relative to a tuned standard PSO baseline. In the industrial case study, the optimized configuration reduced operating cost by 12.4%, lowered carbon emissions by 15.7%, and increased employment by 12.4%; the recurrence of the value 12.4% across the benchmark cost reduction, the case-study cost reduction, and the case-study employment increase is coincidental and not a transcription or copy-paste error: each figure is computed independently from a different quantity (a benchmark average over fifteen instances, an absolute cost change of $18.5M to $16.2M, and a headcount change of 1,247 to 1,402 jobs, respectively), as detailed in the Discussion. All industrial case study improvements are statistically significant (cost and carbon emissions reductions: p < 0.001; employment creation and service-level improvement: p < 0.05; Wilcoxon signed-rank test), as detailed in Table 12. The benchmark instances span regional, multi-regional, large-scale, and extreme-scale network configurations (50 to 500 nodes), with detailed generation parameters and dataset specifications provided in the experimental setup. The proposed QPSO reduced the number of iterations required for convergence by 75.8% compared to standard PSO and achieved up to 3.12× faster runtime for networks with over 500 nodes while maintaining solution quality comparable to or better than the specific tuned metaheuristic baselines evaluated in this study; because no exact (MILP) solver baseline was computed, these solution-quality results are reported relative to those baselines rather than against a certified optimality bound. All benchmark improvements are statistically significant (p < 0.001, Wilcoxon signed-rank test); the bootstrapped 95% confidence interval for the cost-reduction result is [11.4%, 14.0%] (Cohen′s d = 2.84). Real-world validation using data from a global electronics manufacturer indicates practical applicability, with estimated annual cost savings of $2.3M, a 15.7% reduction in carbon emissions, and a 19.4% improvement in network resilience; one-time implementation costs are estimated at $1.83M--$2.43M with a payback period of 9.5--12.7 months. Solution quality on the full 50–500-node suite is reported relative to those tuned metaheuristic baselines; exact-solver verification using the CBC MILP solver on representative small instances (up to 10 nodes; Table 4, Section 5.1.4) confirmed that the model is well-posed and that QPSO solutions fall within 3% of certified optima on those instances. This exact-solver scope is acknowledged as a limitation: verification on instances beyond 10 nodes is computationally intractable with the available hardware, and solution quality for the full benchmark suite is therefore reported relative to identically tuned metaheuristic baselines rather than against certified optima.

title: An accelerated branch-and-cut algorithm for globalized robust sustainable biomass supply-chain optimization under uncertainty
summary: This article addresses the optimal design of a sustainable biomass supply chain under multiple sources of uncertainty, including fluctuating transportation costs and ambiguity in the demand distribution. A globalized robust bi-objective optimization model is proposed that integrates globalized robust optimization for transportation-cost uncertainty with ambiguous chance constraints based on a sub-Gaussian ambiguity set for demand. The model is reformulated as a tractable mixed-integer linear program through robust-counterpart reformulation. To improve computational efficiency, an accelerated branch-and-cut (A-BC) algorithm with problem-specific strengthening inequalities and a warm-start heuristic is developed. Computational experiments based on a Henan Province case with 102 supply points, 46 power plants and 102 candidate collection stations show that the Full A-BC configuration solves the standard test instances within the prescribed time limit and reduces solution time by 51.7% on average relative to the Gurobi-generic-cut baseline across the reported comparable instances. The optimized network yields total cost savings of approximately CNY 6 million compared with a conventional robust model and reduces transportation-related carbon emissions by 6.1% relative to a nominal deterministic model. The proposed approach provides an effective decision-support tool for the design of sustainable biomass supply chains under uncertainty.

title: Driving organizational performance through OHS culture and management in manufacturing SMEs within construction supply chains
summary: Introduction This study examines the relationships among Organizational Culture, Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Management, and Organizational Performance in manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating within construction supply chains in Norte de Santander, Colombia. Methods We collected survey data from 204 employees across 16 manufacturing SMEs and analyzed them using structural equation modeling (SEM). The model evaluated the direct relationships among the three constructs and the indirect effect of Organizational Culture on Organizational Performance through OHS Management. Results The results indicate that Organizational Culture is positively associated with OHS Management and Organizational Performance, while OHS Management is positively associated with Organizational Performance. The bootstrapped indirect effect supports OHS Management's partial mediating role. Discussion These findings suggest that Organizational Culture is associated with performance through two complementary pathways: a direct pathway involving shared values, managerial commitment, communication, and organizational practices, and an indirect pathway involving the institutionalization of OHS management practices. The study contributes to the literature by positioning OHS Management as an organizational mechanism that helps explain how cultural conditions relate to performance outcomes. For manufacturing SMEs linked to construction supply chains, the findings highlight the importance of integrating cultural development with risk prevention, safety training, regulatory compliance, and employee participation. The results should be interpreted considering the cross-sectional design, the use of self-reported data, and the nesting of employees within a limited number of firms.

title: Navigating sustainable performance: the interplay between green dynamic capability, supply chain management, and stakeholder integration
summary: Purpose This study examines the mediating role of green supply chain management practices in the relationship between green dynamic capability and both financial and environmental performance in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Ghana, considering different levels of stakeholder integration. Design/methodology/approach The research employed a quantitative survey design, collecting data from 243 Ghanaian SMEs through a self-administered questionnaire. Data analysis was performed using LISREL 8.80 and Hayes's PROCESS macro with bootstrapping. Findings The findings show that the mediation hypotheses were fully supported: green supply chain management practices significantly mediated the relationship between green dynamic capability and the performance measures. Regarding the conditional indirect effects, no support was found for the hypothesis that stakeholder integration moderates the indirect effect of green dynamic capability on financial performance through green supply chain management practices. However, the results supported the hypothesis that stakeholder integration moderates the indirect effect of green dynamic capability on environmental performance through green supply chain management practices, with stronger effects observed at higher levels of stakeholder integration. These findings contribute to the literature on dynamic capabilities and stakeholder theories by offering new insights into how sustainable practices can enhance performance in SMEs in developing economies. Originality/value These findings add to the literature on dynamic capability and stakeholder theories by offering new insights into how sustainable practices can enhance performance in SMEs within developing economies.

title: Risk-aware hierarchical reinforcement learning for investment and operations in cross-border energy supply chains under the belt and road initiative
summary: Abstract Cross-border energy supply chains under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) face unprecedented challenges, including geopolitical instability, macroeconomic volatility, and operational disruptions. Traditional optimization or flat reinforcement learning (RL) methods often struggle to address the scale, uncertainty, and multi-stakeholder complexity inherent in such environments. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) framework that separates strategic investment planning from tactical operational control via a two-level architecture. The high-level agent makes long-horizon decisions on resource allocation and infrastructure deployment, while the low-level agent handles real-time logistics under dynamically imposed constraints. The framework explicitly incorporates multi-dimensional risk—political, economic, and operational—into both reward shaping and policy learning. Through extensive simulations on representative BRI corridors, the proposed HRL model demonstrates superior simulated performance over single-level RL, mixed-integer programming, and rule-based baselines across key metrics, including cumulative profit (+ 25%), service-level reliability, and robustness to stress scenarios. Ablation and continual learning experiments further confirm the contributions of hierarchical abstraction and risk-aware training. This work contributes a scalable, interpretable, and risk-resilient decision-making architecture for intelligent energy infrastructure planning in global contexts.

title: Smart City Pilot Programs and the Advancement of the Digital Economy: Empirical Insights from China
summary: Abstract In recent years, China has experienced rapid urbanization and technological advancement, with particular emphasis on the development of smart cities. A smart city integrates advanced technologies to enhance overall efficiency, improve the quality of urban services, and foster economic development. As part of this broader trend, various Chinese cities have initiated smart city pilot programs to explore the potential benefits of integrating digital technologies into urban management. Against this backdrop, this article seeks to assess the impact of smart city pilots on the development of the digital economy in China. Based on panel data from 285 Chinese cities at the prefecture level or above between 2011 and 2019, this article employs a difference-in-differences method to evaluate the impact of smart city pilots on the development of the digital economy. The research findings indicate that on average, smart city pilots significantly enhance the level of digital economy development by 0.756%. Smart city pilots can affect the development of the digital economy through mechanisms such as digital consumption, information collection, and human capital. These conclusions provide significant policy references for accelerating the construction of smart cities and promoting the development of the digital economy in China in the new era.

title: Evidence from China: A quantitative examination of China's new competition regime for the digital economy
summary: Growing global concern about the problems associated with concentrated market power in the digital economy is leading to a renewed interest in competition policy. Since the late 2010s, China’s government has squarely confronted the problems of its own ‘Big Tech’ with a new competition regime for digital markets. The ensuing ‘tech crackdown’ of late 2020 provides a rare quasi-natural experiment to study the impact of antitrust regulation. Here we deploy a novel market capitalization approach that builds on the informativeness of China’s financial markets. Harnessing Bloomberg data of 1142 publicly listed firms for the period 2019 to 2022, we find that across China's digital economy, this unprecedented intervention is associated with both reduced market concentration and reduced market-capitalization growth, but no harms to revenue. Employing a difference-in-differences and event-study design, we identify a causal link between China’s new competition regime and a reduction in concentration in the primary markets of China's three most dominant digital platforms — Baidu, Alibaba and Tencent (BATs). Other empirical findings include a negative association between market concentration and the openness of digital markets and a non-relationship between market concentration and profits. Our results indicate that neither profit- nor revenue-based metrics are entirely appropriate for measuring digital market power effectively. We conclude by discussing the relative success of China’s digital competition policy as well as the relevance of these insights for global, including Western regulatory strategies.

title: SYSTEM OF STATE GOVERNANCE MECHANISMS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF INNOVATIVE ENTREPRENEURSHIP UNDER THE CONDITIONS OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF SOCIETY
summary: The article provides a comprehensive theoretical, methodological, and applied study of the formation and functioning of the system of state management mechanisms for the development of innovative entrepreneurship under the conditions of the total digital transformation of society. The essential and substantive characteristics of innovative entrepreneurship as a leading driver of national economic modernization are investigated. It is determined that digitalization acts as a catalyst for transformational processes, radically changing the architecture of business models, market structures, and tools of state regulatory policy. Based on a systematic approach, the system of state management mechanisms is structured into key blocks: regulatory, financial-economic, organizational-managerial, and information-technological. Special attention is paid to the analysis of the current state and trends in the development of innovative entrepreneurship in Ukraine. The dynamics of key indicators of innovative activity of domestic enterprises during 2018-2025 are analyzed, including the share of enterprises implementing innovations, the volume of funding for research and development (R&D), and the level of digital maturity of the business environment. Key destructive factors and barriers hindering innovative activity in the national space under martial law and post-war recovery are identified. The advanced experience of the European Union countries is studied in detail, in particular the models of Germany (the industrial platform 'Industry 4.0'), Estonia (the concept of the digital state 'e-Estonia' and digitalization of public services), and Finland (the ecosystem approach and financing tools of the Business Finland agency). The best European practices regarding the development of a network of digital innovation hubs, stimulation of venture investment, and implementation of tax incentives for knowledge-intensive enterprises are highlighted. A conceptual model for the modernization of public administration is proposed, which involves the integration of European standards, the expansion of public-private partnership instruments, the digitalization of administrative services for business, and the creation of a favorable regulatory landscape (regulatory 'sandboxes'). It is substantiated that the implementation of the proposed recommendations will ensure increasing the competitiveness of the national economy, accelerating European integration processes, and sustainable technological development of society.

title: Leading AI-Driven Digital Transformation: A Review of Leadership Attributes and Practices, with Implications for Singapore
summary: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how enterprises are led, organised, and governed, raising critical questions about which leadership attributes and practices best enable AI-driven digital transformation (AIDT). Enterprises face growing pressure to accelerate AIDT in Asian countries such as Singapore, with stakeholders demanding tangible returns from AI investments, though there is limited clarity on the leadership attributes and practices that enable such success. Drawing on an integrated theoretical lens that synthesises theories of transformational leadership, ambidextrous leadership, and dynamic capabilities, this paper systematically reviews 73 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and thematically synthesises the evidence into an integrated leadership framework for AIDT. The synthesis identifies seven leadership attributes, four strategic priorities, six organisational focus areas for AI exploration, and six integrated AI governance practices. This review reports valuable findings on navigating AIDT with key leadership attributes and practices that balance innovation, accountability, and sustainability. The study contributes to the leadership and digital transformation literature by clarifying how leadership orchestrates the interplay between technology, practices, and governance in AIDT, and by proposing a research agenda for empirically validating the framework derived across various industry contexts.

title: EDUCATING PHYSICIANS FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: MEDICAL UNIVERSITIES IN UZBEKISTAN AND SAFE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN HEALTHCARE
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming healthcare delivery, clinical decision-making and health system governance. However, the safety and effectiveness of AI implementation depend not only on technological infrastructure but also on workforce preparedness and institutional capacity. This conceptual study explores the role of medical universities in Uzbekistan in developing competencies required for responsible AI adoption in clinical practice, healthcare management and public health. Drawing on international literature, policy frameworks and national academic discourse, the paper proposes a conceptual model explaining how educational interventions influence professional readiness for safe AI integration. The analysis highlights persistentcompetency gaps, the mediating role of universities in shaping professional attitudes and broader system-level implications of AI literacy programmes. The study argues that competency-oriented educational strategies aligned with national digital health reforms may support sustainable innovation while preserving professional accountability and patient safety.
